1.38.e: Now if he had said: " Let us sing both with the re and with the sāman," truly he would have told them: " Sing with a sucked-out, used-up branch of the a»iate-plant." Therefore he spoke thus: " Let us sing both with tone and with the hinkdra."
1.38.m: Now if he had said, 'We sang with the ṛc and with the sāman,' he would have said to them: 'You sang with what is already drunk, with what has lost its freshness, with a stem of amalā.' But he said this: 'We sang with the musical tone and with the hiṅkāra.' // Third [recte fourth] khaṇḍa in the twelfth anuvāka

1.39.s: atha ha satyādhivākaś caitrarathis satyayajñam pauluṣitam uvāca prācīnayogeti mama ced vai tvaṃ sāma vidvān sāmnārtvijyaṃ kariṣyasi naiva tarhi punar dīkṣām abhidhyātāsīti muhurdīkṣī hy āsa |
1.39.d: अथ ह सत्याधिवाकश् चैत्ररथिस् सत्ययज्ञम् पौलुषितम् उवाच प्राचीनयोगेति मम चेद् वै त्वं साम विद्वान् साम्नार्त्विज्यं करिष्यसि नैव तर्हि पुनर् दीक्षाम् अभिध्यातासीति मुहुर्दीक्षी ह्य् आस ।
1.39.e: Now Satyadhivaka Caitrarathi said to Satyayajfia Paulusita: " O Pracinayoga, if thou, knowing the sāman, shalt perform the priestly office for me with the sdtnan, then thou wilt not think of a second consecration." For he was one who repeatedly consecrated.
1.39.m: Now Satyādhivāka Caitrarathi said to Satyayajña Pauluṣita: 'Prācīnayoga, if you, knowing my sāman, perform the priestly office with the sāman, you will not intend to take the consecration again!' For he used to take consecration repeatedly.

1.39.s: sa hovāca yo vai sāmnaś śriyaṃ vidvān sāmnārtvijyaṃ karoti śrīmān eva bhavati mano vāva sāmnaś śrīr iti |
1.39.d: स होवाच यो वै साम्नश् श्रियं विद्वान् साम्नार्त्विज्यं करोति श्रीमान् एव भवति मनो वाव साम्नश् श्रीर् इति ।
1.39.e: He said: "He who knowing the fortune of the sāman performs the priestly office with the sāman, he becomes fortunate. Verily mind is the fortune of the sāman.
1.39.m: He said: 'He who, knowing the prosperity of the sāman, performs the priestly office with the sāman becomes prosperous. Mind, indeed, is the prosperity of the sāman.'

1.39.s: yo vai sāmnaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ vidvān sāmnārtvijyaṃ karoti praty eva tiṣṭhati vāg vāva sāmnaḥ pratiṣṭheti |
1.39.d: यो वै साम्नः प्रतिष्ठां विद्वान् साम्नार्त्विज्यं करोति प्रत्य् एव तिष्ठति वाग् वाव साम्नः प्रतिष्ठेति ।
1.39.e: He who knowing the firm stand of the sāman performs the priestlj' office with the sāman, he stands firm. Verily speech is the firm stand of the sāman.
1.39.m: 'He who, knowing the firm foundation of the sāman, performs the priestly office with the sāman becomes firmly established. Speech, indeed, is the firm foundation of the sāman.'

1.39.s: yo vai sāmnas suvarṇaṃ vidvān sāmnārtvijyaṃ karoty adhy asya gṛhe suvarṇaṃ gamyate prāṇo vāva sāmnas suvarṇam iti |
1.39.d: यो वै साम्नस् सुवर्णं विद्वान् साम्नार्त्विज्यं करोत्य् अध्य् अस्य गृहे सुवर्णं गम्यते प्राणो वाव साम्नस् सुवर्णम् इति ।
1.39.e: He who knowing the gold of the sāman performs the priestly office with the sāman, in his house gold is found. Verily breath is the gold of the sāman.
1.39.m: 'He who, knowing the gold of the sāman, performs the priestly office with the sāman—gold is found in his house. Breath, indeed, is the gold of the sāman.'

1.39.s: yo vai sāmno 'pacitiṃ vidvān sāmnārtvijyaṃ karoty apacitimān eva bhavati cakṣur vāva sāmno 'pacitir iti |
1.39.d: यो वै साम्नो ऽपचितिं विद्वान् साम्नार्त्विज्यं करोत्य् अपचितिमान् एव भवति चक्षुर् वाव साम्नो ऽपचितिर् इति ।
1.39.e: He who knowing the reverence of the sāman performs the priestly office with the sāman, he becomes revered. Verily sight is the reverence of the sāman.
1.39.m: 'He who, knowing the honor of the sāman, performs the priestly office with the sāman becomes honored. The eye, indeed, is the honor of the sāman.'

1.39.s: yo vai sāmnaś śrutiṃ vidvān sāmnārtvijyaṃ karoti śrutimān eva bhavati śrotraṃ vāva sāmnaś śrutir iti | dvādaśe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ dvādaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
1.39.d: यो वै साम्नश् श्रुतिं विद्वान् साम्नार्त्विज्यं करोति श्रुतिमान् एव भवति श्रोत्रं वाव साम्नश् श्रुतिर् इति । द्वादशे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः द्वादशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
1.39.e: He who knowing the renown of the sāman performs the priestly office with the sāman, he becomes renowned. Verily hearing is the renown of the sāman.
1.39.m: 'He who, knowing the fame of the sāman, performs the priestly office with the sāman becomes famous. The ear, indeed, is the fame of the sāman.' // Fourth [recte fifth] khaṇḍa in the twelfth anuvāka. The twelfth anuvāka is completed.

1.40.s: catvāri vāk parimitā padāni tāni vidur brāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṃ vāco manuṣyā vadantī ti |
1.40.d: चत्वारि वाक् परिमिता पदानि तानि विदुर् ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः गुहा त्रीणि निहिता नेङ्गयन्ति तुरीयं वाचो मनुष्या वदन्ती ति ।
1.40.m: 'Speech is measured in four quarters; wise brahmins know them. / Three, placed in secret, do not stir; mortals speak the fourth of speech.'

1.40.s: vāg eva sāma vācā hi sāma gāyati vāg evoktham vācā hy ukthaṃ śaṃsati vāg eva yajuḥ vācā hi yajur anuvartate |
1.40.d: वाग् एव साम वाचा हि साम गायति वाग् एवोक्थम् वाचा ह्य् उक्थं शंसति वाग् एव यजुः वाचा हि यजुर् अनुवर्तते ।
1.40.e: Speech is the sāman; for with speech one sings the sāman. Speech is the uklha; for with speech one ch-ants the uktha. Speech is the yajus; for with speech he follows out (recites) the yajits.
1.40.m: Speech is the sāman, for with speech one sings the sāman. Speech is the uktha, for with speech one recites the uktha. Speech is the yajus, for with speech one follows along with the yajus.

1.40.s: tad yat kiṃ cārvācīnam brahmaṇas tad vāg eva sarvam atha yad anyatra brahmopadiśyate naiva hi tenārtvijyaṃ karoti parokṣeṇaiva tu kṛtam bhavati |
1.40.d: तद् यत् किं चार्वाचीनम् ब्रह्मणस् तद् वाग् एव सर्वम् अथ यद् अन्यत्र ब्रह्मोपदिश्यते नैव हि तेनार्त्विज्यं करोति परोक्षेणैव तु कृतम् भवति ।
1.40.e: W hatsoever is this side of the brahman, all that is speech; and what is elsewhere is taught [to be] brahman. For not at all does one perform with it the priestly office, but it is performed in an occult manner.
1.40.m: Whatever is on this side of brahman, all that is speech alone. Now, as for brahman being taught elsewhere: one does not perform the priestly office with it, but it is done only indirectly.

1.40.s: tasyā etasyai vāco manaḥ pādaś cakṣuḥ pādaś śrotram pādo vāg eva caturthaḥ pādaḥ |
1.40.d: तस्या एतस्यै वाचो मनः पादश् चक्षुः पादश् श्रोत्रम् पादो वाग् एव चतुर्थः पादः ।
1.40.e: Of this same speech mind is a quarter, sight is a quarter, hearing is a quarter, speech itself is the fourth quarter.
1.40.m: Of this speech, the mind is a quarter, the eye is a quarter, the ear is a quarter, speech itself is the fourth quarter.

1.40.s: tad yad vai manasā dhyāyati tad vācā vadati yac cakṣuṣā paśyati tad vācā vadati yac chrotreṇa śṛṇoti tad vācā vadati |
1.40.d: तद् यद् वै मनसा ध्यायति तद् वाचा वदति यच् चक्षुषा पश्यति तद् वाचा वदति यच् छ्रोत्रेण शृणोति तद् वाचा वदति ।
1.40.e: What he thinks with the mind, that he speaks with speech. What he sees with sight, that he speaks with speech. What he hears with hearing, that he speaks with speech.
1.40.m: For what one thinks with the mind, that one speaks with speech; what one sees with the eye, that one speaks with speech; what one hears with the ear, that one speaks with speech.

1.40.s: tad yad etat sarvaṃ vācam evābhisamayati tasmād vāg eva sāma sa ha vai sāmavit sa sāma veda ya evaṃ veda |
1.40.d: तद् यद् एतत् सर्वं वाचम् एवाभिसमयति तस्माद् वाग् एव साम स ह वै सामवित् स साम वेद य एवं वेद ।
1.40.e: In that this all thus unites (,y/i + sam) into speech, therefore speech is the sāman. Verily he is samaw-knowing, he knows the sāman, who knows thus.
1.40.m: Since all this merges into speech alone, therefore speech is the sāman. He is indeed a knower of the sāman, he knows the sāman, who knows thus.

1.40.s: tasyā etasyai vācaḥ prāṇā evāsuḥ eṣu hīdaṃ sarvam asūteti | trayodaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.40.d: तस्या एतस्यै वाचः प्राणा एवासुः एषु हीदं सर्वम् असूतेति । त्रयोदशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
1.40.e: The breaths of this same speech are the vital air [asu). For in them this all was born (Śsic).
1.40.m: Of this speech, the breaths are the vital life, for in them all this was brought forth. // First khaṇḍa in the thirteenth anuvāka

1.41.s: tena haitenāsunā devā jīvanti pitaro jīvanti manuṣyā jīvanti paśavo jīvanti gandharvāpsaraso jīvanti sarvam idaṃ jīvati |
1.41.d: तेन हैतेनासुना देवा जीवन्ति पितरो जीवन्ति मनुष्या जीवन्ति पशवो जीवन्ति गन्धर्वाप्सरसो जीवन्ति सर्वम् इदं जीवति ।
1.41.e: By this same vital air the gods live, the Fathers live, men live, beasts live, Gandharvas and Apsarases live, this all lives.
1.41.m: By this vital life the gods live, the ancestors live, humans live, beasts live, gandharvas and apsarases live; all this lives.

1.41.s: tad āhur yad asunedaṃ sarvaṃ jīvati kas sāmno 'sur iti prāṇa iti brūyāt prāṇo ha vāva sāmno 'suḥ |
1.41.d: तद् आहुर् यद् असुनेदं सर्वं जीवति कस् साम्नो ऽसुर् इति प्राण इति ब्रूयात् प्राणो ह वाव साम्नो ऽसुः ।
1.41.e: This they say: " If this all lives by the vital air, what is the vital air of the sāman?" Let him say: " Breath." Verily breath is the vital air of the sāman.
1.41.m: Regarding this they say: 'Since everything lives by life-breath, what is the life-breath of the sāman?' He should say: 'Breath.' Breath, indeed, is the life-breath of the sāman.

1.41.s: sa eṣa prāṇo vāci pratiṣṭhito vāg u prāṇe pratiṣṭhitā tāv etāv evam anyo 'nyasmin pratiṣṭhitau pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda |
1.41.d: स एष प्राणो वाचि प्रतिष्ठितो वाग् उ प्राणे प्रतिष्ठिता ताव् एताव् एवम् अन्यो ऽन्यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितौ प्रतितिष्ठति य एवं वेद ।
1.41.e: This breath stands firm in speech, and speech stands firm in breath. Thus these two stand firm in each other. He stands firm who knows thus.
1.41.m: This breath is established in speech, and speech is established in breath. In this way, these two are established in one another. He who knows this thus becomes established.

1.41.s: tad etad ṛcābhyanūcyate 'ditir dyaur aditir antarikṣam aditir mātā sa pitā sa putraḥ viśve devā aditiḥ pañca janā aditir jātam aditir janitvam iti |
1.41.d: तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्यनूच्यते ऽदितिर् द्यौर् अदितिर् अन्तरिक्षम् अदितिर् माता स पिता स पुत्रः विश्वे देवा अदितिः पञ्च जना अदितिर् जातम् अदितिर् जनित्वम् इति ।
1.41.e: This same is spoken of in a re: " Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is the atmosphere, Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son; Aditi is all the gods, the five races; Aditi is what is born, Aditi is what is to be born."
1.41.m:
This is referred to in a verse:
'Aditi is heaven, Aditi is intermediate space, Aditi is mother, she is father, she is son.
Aditi is all the gods, the five peoples, Aditi is what is born, Aditi is what is to be born.'

1.41.s: aditir dyaur aditir antarikṣam iti eṣā vai dyaur eṣāntarikṣam |
1.41.d: अदितिर् द्यौर् अदितिर् अन्तरिक्षम् इति एषा वै द्यौर् एषान्तरिक्षम् ।
1.41.e: ' Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is the atmosphere;' verily she is the heaven, she is the atmosphere.
1.41.m: 'Aditi is heaven, Aditi is intermediate space'—this [speech] indeed is heaven, this is intermediate space.

1.41.s: aditir mātā sa pitā sa putra iti eṣā vai mātaiṣā pitaiṣā putraḥ |
1.41.d: अदितिर् माता स पिता स पुत्र इति एषा वै मातैषा पितैषा पुत्रः ।
1.41.e: ' Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son;' verily she is the mother, she is the father, she is the son.
1.41.m: 'Aditi is mother, she is father, she is son'—this indeed is mother, this is father, this is son.

1.41.s: viśve devā aditiḥ pañca janā iti ye devā asurebhyaḥ pūrve pañca janā āsan ya evāsāv āditye puruṣo yaś candramasi yo vidyuti yo 'psu yo 'yam akṣann antar eṣa eva te tad eṣaiva |
1.41.d: विश्वे देवा अदितिः पञ्च जना इति ये देवा असुरेभ्यः पूर्वे पञ्च जना आसन् य एवासाव् आदित्ये पुरुषो यश् चन्द्रमसि यो विद्युति यो ऽप्सु यो ऽयम् अक्षन्न् अन्तर् एष एव ते तद् एषैव ।
1.41.e: 'Aditi is all the gods, the five races;' the gods who were befoi-e the Asuras—five races— yonder person which is in the sun, in the moon, in lightning, in the water, within the eye here, that is they, that is she.
1.41.m: 'Aditi is all the gods, the five peoples'—the gods who were the five peoples prior to the asuras: the person who is in the sun, who is in the moon, who is in lightning, who is in the waters, who is here within the eye—he indeed is they. Therefore, she is all this.

1.41.s: aditir jātam aditir janitvam iti eṣā hy eva jātam eṣā janitvam | trayodaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ trayodaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
1.41.d: अदितिर् जातम् अदितिर् जनित्वम् इति एषा ह्य् एव जातम् एषा जनित्वम् । त्रयोदशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः त्रयोदशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
1.41.e: ' Aditi is what is born, Aditi is what is to be born;' verily she is what is born, she is what is to be born.
1.41.m:
'Aditi is what is born, Aditi is what is to be born'—for she indeed is what is born, she is what is to be born.
Second khaṇḍa in the thirteenth anuvāka.
The thirteenth anuvāka is completed.

1.42.s: āruṇir ha vāsiṣṭhaṃ caikitāneyam brahmacaryam upeyāya taṃ hovācājānāsi saumya gautama yad idaṃ vayaṃ caikitāneyās sāmaivopāsmahe kāṃ tvaṃ devatām upāssa iti sāmaiva bhagavanta iti hovāca |
1.42.d: आरुणिर् ह वासिष्ठं चैकितानेयम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् उपेयाय तं होवाचाजानासि सौम्य गौतम यद् इदं वयं चैकितानेयास् सामैवोपास्महे कां त्वं देवताम् उपास्स इति सामैव भगवन्त इति होवाच ।
1.42.e: Aruni went to Vfisistha _Caikitaneya to serve his studentship. He (V.) said to him (A.): "Thou knowest, my dear Gautama, that we Caikitfmeyas worship this sāman. What divinity dost thou worship?" " The sdnian, reverend sirs," he (A.) said.
1.42.m: Āruṇi approached Vāsiṣṭha Caikitāneya as a Vedic student. He said to him: 'Do you know, gentle Gautama, that we Caikitāneyas worship the sāman alone? Which deity do you worship?' He said: 'The sāman alone, venerable sir.'

1.42.s: taṃ ha papraccha yad agnau tad vetthā3 iti jyotir vā etat tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.42.d: तं ह पप्रच्छ यद् अग्नौ तद् वेत्था3 इति ज्योतिर् वा एतत् तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.42.e: He (A.) asked him (V.): "Dost thou know that which is in the fire?" " That is the brightness of that sāman which we worship."
1.42.m: He asked him: 'Do you know what is in Agni?' [He replied:] 'It is the light of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.42.s: yat pṛthivyāṃ tad vetthā3 iti pratiṣṭhā vā eṣā tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.42.d: यत् पृथिव्यां तद् वेत्था3 इति प्रतिष्ठा वा एषा तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.42.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the earth?" "That is the firm standing of that sāman yihioh we worship."
1.42.m: 'Do you know what is in the earth?' [He replied:] 'It is the foundation of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.42.s: yad apsu tad vetthā3 iti śāntir vā eṣā tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.42.d: यद् अप्सु तद् वेत्था3 इति शान्तिर् वा एषा तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.42.e: "Dost thou know that which is in the waters?" "That is the tranquillity of that sāman which we worship."
1.42.m: 'Do you know what is in the waters?' [He replied:] 'It is the peace of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.42.s: yad antarikṣe tad vetthā3 iti ātmā vā eṣa tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.42.d: यद् अन्तरिक्षे तद् वेत्था3 इति आत्मा वा एष तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.42.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the atmosphere?" " That is the self of that sāman which we worship."
1.42.m: 'Do you know what is in the intermediate space?' [He replied:] 'It is the self of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.42.s: yad vāyau tad vetthā3 iti śrīr vā eṣā tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.42.d: यद् वायौ तद् वेत्था3 इति श्रीर् वा एषा तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.42.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the wind?" " That is the fortune of that sāman which we worship."
1.42.m: 'Do you know what is in Vāyu?' [He replied:] 'It is the glory of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.42.s: yad dikṣu tad vetthā3 iti vyāptir vā eṣā tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.42.d: यद् दिक्षु तद् वेत्था3 इति व्याप्तिर् वा एषा तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.42.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the quarters?" " That is the pervasion of that sāman which we worship."
1.42.m: 'Do you know what is in the directions?' [He replied:] 'It is the pervasion of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.42.s: yad divi tad vetthā3 iti vibhūtir vā eṣā tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti | caturdaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.42.d: यद् दिवि तद् वेत्था3 इति विभूतिर् वा एषा तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति । चतुर्दशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
1.42.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the sky?" " That is the display of that sāman which we worship."
1.42.m:
'Do you know what is in heaven?' [He replied:] 'It is the manifestation of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'
First khaṇḍa in the fourteenth anuvāka.

1.43.s: yad āditye tad vetthā3 iti tejo vā etat tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.43.d: यद् आदित्ये तद् वेत्था3 इति तेजो वा एतत् तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.43.e: "Dost thou know that which is in the sun?" "That is the splendor of that sāman which we worship."
1.43.m: 'Do you know what is in the sun?' [He replied:] 'It is the splendor of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.43.s: yac candramasi tad vetthā3 iti bhā vā eṣā tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.43.d: यच् चन्द्रमसि तद् वेत्था3 इति भा वा एषा तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.43.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the moon?" " That is the light of that sāman which we worship."
1.43.m: 'Do you know what is in the moon?' [He replied:] 'It is the luster of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.43.s: yan nakṣatreṣu tad vetthā3 iti prajñā vā eṣā tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.43.d: यन् नक्षत्रेषु तद् वेत्था3 इति प्रज्ञा वा एषा तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.43.e: "Dost thou know that which is in the asterisms?" " That is the understanding of that sāman which we worship."
1.43.m: 'Do you know what is in the stars?' [He replied:] 'It is the wisdom of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.43.s: yad anne tad vetthā3 iti reto vā etat tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.43.d: यद् अन्ने तद् वेत्था3 इति रेतो वा एतत् तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.43.e: "Dost thou know that which is in food?" " That is the seed of that sāman which we worship."
1.43.m: 'Do you know what is in food?' [He replied:] 'It is the semen of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.43.s: yat paśuṣu tad vetthā3 iti yaśo vā etat tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.43.d: यत् पशुषु तद् वेत्था3 इति यशो वा एतत् तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.43.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the domestic animals?" " That is the glory of that sāman which we worship."
1.43.m: 'Do you know what is in cattle?' [He replied:] 'It is the fame of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.43.s: yad ṛci tad vetthā3 iti stomo vā eṣa tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.43.d: यद् ऋचि तद् वेत्था3 इति स्तोमो वा एष तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.43.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the re?" " That is the praise of that sāman which we worship."
1.43.m: 'Do you know what is in the ṛc?' [He replied:] 'It is the stoma of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.43.s: yad yajuṣi tad vetthā3 iti karma vā etat tasya sāmno yad vayaṃ sāmopāsmaha iti |
1.43.d: यद् यजुषि तद् वेत्था3 इति कर्म वा एतत् तस्य साम्नो यद् वयं सामोपास्मह इति ।
1.43.e: " Dost thou know that which is in Xh^yajus?" "That is the action of that sāman which we worship."'
1.43.m: 'Do you know what is in the yajus?' [He replied:] 'It is the ritual action of that sāman, which we worship as the sāman.'

1.43.s: atha kim upāssa iti akṣaram iti katamat tad akṣaram iti yat kṣaran nākṣīyateti katamat tat kṣaran nākṣīyateti indra iti |
1.43.d: अथ किम् उपास्स इति अक्षरम् इति कतमत् तद् अक्षरम् इति यत् क्षरन् नाक्षीयतेति कतमत् तत् क्षरन् नाक्षीयतेति इन्द्र इति ।
1.43.e: " Now what dost thou worship?" " The syllable." " Which is that syllable?" " [That] which flowing {^/ksar) was not exhausted (AJksi)." "Which is that which flowing was not exhausted?" "Indra."
1.43.m: 'Then what do you worship?' 'The syllable / imperishable.' 'Which is that syllable / imperishable?' 'That which, while trickling, does not perish.' 'Which is that which, while trickling, does not perish?' 'Indra.'

1.43.s: katamas sa indra iti yo 'kṣan ramata iti katamas sa yo 'kṣan ramata iti iyaṃ devateti hovāca |
1.43.d: कतमस् स इन्द्र इति यो ऽक्षन् रमत इति कतमस् स यो ऽक्षन् रमत इति इयं देवतेति होवाच ।
1.43.e: "Who is this Indra?" "He who rests in the eye." " Who is he who rests in the eye?" "This divinity," he said.
1.43.m: 'Which is that Indra?' 'He who revels in the eye.' 'Which is that one who revels in the eye?' 'This deity,' he said.

1.43.s: yo 'yaṃ cakṣuṣi puruṣa eṣa indra eṣa prajāpatiḥ samaḥ pṛthivyā sama ākāśena samo divā samas sarveṇa bhūtena eṣa paro divo dīpyate eṣa evedaṃ sarvam ity upāsitavyaḥ |
1.43.d: यो ऽयं चक्षुषि पुरुष एष इन्द्र एष प्रजापतिः समः पृथिव्या सम आकाशेन समो दिवा समस् सर्वेण भूतेन एष परो दिवो दीप्यते एष एवेदं सर्वम् इत्य् उपासितव्यः ।
1.43.e: That person which is in the eye, that is Indra, that is Prajapati. [He is] the same with the earth, the same with space, the same with the sky, the same with all existence. He shines beyond the sky. He it is who must be worshiped as 'this all.'
1.43.m: 'This person who is here in the eye—he is Indra, he is Prajāpati. He is equal to the earth, equal to space, equal to heaven, equal to all existence. He shines beyond heaven. He alone is all this: thus should he be worshipped.'

1.43.s: sa ya etad evaṃ veda jyotiṣmān pratiṣṭhāvāñ chāntimān ātmavāñ chrīmān vyāptimān vibhūtimāṃs tejasvī bhāvān prajñāvān retasvī yaśasvī stomavān karmavān akṣaravān indriyavān sāmanvī bhavati |
1.43.d: स य एतद् एवं वेद ज्योतिष्मान् प्रतिष्ठावाञ् छान्तिमान् आत्मवाञ् छ्रीमान् व्याप्तिमान् विभूतिमांस् तेजस्वी भावान् प्रज्ञावान् रेतस्वी यशस्वी स्तोमवान् कर्मवान् अक्षरवान् इन्द्रियवान् सामन्वी भवति ।
1.43.e: He who knows this thus becomes bright, having a firm stand, tranquil, self-possessed, fortunate, pervading, displayed, possessing splendor, possessing light, possessing understanding, possessing seed, glorious, possessing praise, active, possessing the syllable, possessing Indra's power, possessing the sāman.
1.43.m: He who knows this thus becomes luminous, possessing a foundation, possessing peace, possessing a self, possessing glory, possessing pervasion, possessing manifestation, possessing splendor, possessing luster, possessing wisdom, possessing semen, possessing fame, possessing stomas, possessing ritual action, possessing the syllable / imperishable, possessing sensory power, possessing the sāman.

1.43.s: tad v etad ṛcābhyanūcyate | caturdaśame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.43.d: तद् व् एतद् ऋचाभ्यनूच्यते । चतुर्दशमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
1.43.e: And this is also spoken of in a re:
1.43.m:
And this is also referred to in a verse.
Second khaṇḍa in the fourteenth anuvāka.

1.44.s: rūpaṃ-rūpam pratirūpo babhūva tad asya rūpam praticakṣaṇāya indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hy asya harayaś śatā daśeti |
1.44.d: रूपं-रूपम् प्रतिरूपो बभूव तद् अस्य रूपम् प्रतिचक्षणाय इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्य् अस्य हरयश् शता दशेति ।
1.44.e: "He became corresponding in form to every form; such is his form to look upon; Indra through magic moves about in many forms, for his ten hundred bay steeds are yoked."
1.44.m:
'In every form he has become the counterpart form; that is his form to look upon.
Indra moves in many forms by his magic arts, for his ten hundred bay steeds are yoked.'

1.44.s: rūpaṃ-rūpam pratirūpo babhūveti rūpaṃ-rūpaṃ hy eṣa pratirūpo babhūva |
1.44.d: रूपं-रूपम् प्रतिरूपो बभूवेति रूपं-रूपं ह्य् एष प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
1.44.e: ' He became corresponding in form to every form,' for he became corresponding in form to every form.
1.44.m: 'In every form he has become the counterpart form'—for in every form he has become the counterpart form.

1.44.s: tad asya rūpam praticakṣaṇāyeti praticakṣaṇāya hāsyaitad rūpam |
1.44.d: तद् अस्य रूपम् प्रतिचक्षणायेति प्रतिचक्षणाय हास्यैतद् रूपम् ।
1.44.e: 'Such is his form to look upon,' verily to look upon his form is such.
1.44.m: 'That is his form to look upon'—for this form of his is for looking upon.

1.44.s: indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyata iti māyābhir hy eṣa etat pururūpa īyate |
1.44.d: इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयत इति मायाभिर् ह्य् एष एतत् पुरुरूप ईयते ।
1.44.e: ' Indra through magic moves about in many forms,' for through magic he thus moves about in many forms.
1.44.m: 'Indra moves in many forms by his magic arts'—for by his magic arts he moves in many forms in this way.

1.44.s: yuktā hy asya harayaś śatā daśeti sahasraṃ haita ādityasya raśmayaḥ te 'sya yuktās tair idaṃ sarvaṃ harati tad yad etair idaṃ sarvaṃ harati tasmād dharayaḥ |
1.44.d: युक्ता ह्य् अस्य हरयश् शता दशेति सहस्रं हैत आदित्यस्य रश्मयः ते ऽस्य युक्तास् तैर् इदं सर्वं हरति तद् यद् एतैर् इदं सर्वं हरति तस्माद् धरयः ।
1.44.e: ' For his ten hundred bay steeds are yoked,' verily these are the thousand rays of the sun; they are yoked for him, with them he takes this all. In that he takes (/\/hr) with them this all, therefore they are called bay {hari).
1.44.m: 'For his ten hundred bay steeds are yoked'—these are indeed the thousand rays of the sun. They are yoked to him; by them he carries away (harati) all this. Because he carries away all this by them, therefore they are bay steeds (harayaḥ).

1.44.s: rūpaṃ-rūpam maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānaḥ pari tanvaṃ svām trir yad divaḥ pari muhūrtam āgāt svair mantrair anṛtupā ṛtāveti |
1.44.d: रूपं-रूपम् मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानः परि तन्वं स्वाम् त्रिर् यद् दिवः परि मुहूर्तम् आगात् स्वैर् मन्त्रैर् अनृतुपा ऋतावेति ।
1.44.e: "Into every form the bounteous one often changes, exercising magic around his own body, when thrice in a moment he hath come from the sky, through his own incantations drinking out of season, the holy one."
1.44.m:
'Maghavan repeatedly takes form after form, making magic arts around his own body,
when thrice from heaven he has come around in a moment, drinking out of season by his own mantras, true to the cosmic order.'

1.44.s: rūpaṃ-rūpam maghavā bobhavītīti rūpaṃ-rūpaṃ hy eṣa maghavā bobhavīti |
1.44.d: रूपं-रूपम् मघवा बोभवीतीति रूपं-रूपं ह्य् एष मघवा बोभवीति ।
1.44.e: ' Into every form the bounteous one often changes,' for into every form this bounteous one does often change,
1.44.m: 'Maghavan repeatedly takes form after form'—for Maghavan repeatedly takes form after form.

1.44.s: māyāḥ kṛṇvānaḥ pari tanvaṃ svām iti māyābhir hy eṣa etat svāṃ tanuṃ gopāyati |
1.44.d: मायाः कृण्वानः परि तन्वं स्वाम् इति मायाभिर् ह्य् एष एतत् स्वां तनुं गोपायति ।
1.44.e: ' Exercising magic around his own body,' for through magic he thus protects his own body.
1.44.m: 'Making magic arts around his own body'—for by magic arts he protects his own body in this way.

1.44.s: trir yad divaḥ pari muhūrtam āgād iti trir ha vā eṣa etasya muhūrtasyemām pṛthivīṃ samantaḥ paryetīmāḥ prajās saṃcakṣāṇaḥ |
1.44.d: त्रिर् यद् दिवः परि मुहूर्तम् आगाद् इति त्रिर् ह वा एष एतस्य मुहूर्तस्येमाम् पृथिवीं समन्तः पर्येतीमाः प्रजास् संचक्षाणः ।
1.44.e: ' When he thrice in a moment hath come from the sky,' for thrice in this moment he goes completely around this earth surveying these people,
1.44.m: 'When thrice from heaven he has come around in a moment'—thrice indeed in this moment he goes around this earth on all sides, observing these creatures.

1.44.s: svair mantrair anṛtupā ṛtāveti anṛtupā hy eṣa etad ṛtāvā | caturdaśe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.44.d: स्वैर् मन्त्रैर् अनृतुपा ऋतावेति अनृतुपा ह्य् एष एतद् ऋतावा । चतुर्दशे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
1.44.e: ' Through his own incantations drinking out of season, the holy one,' for he is thus drinking out of season, the holy one.
1.44.m:
'Drinking out of season by his own mantras, true to the cosmic order'—for drinking out of season, he is in this way true to the cosmic order.
Third khaṇḍa in the fourteenth anuvāka.

1.45.s: tad dha pṛthur vainyo divyān vrātyān papracche indram uktham ṛcam udgītham āhur brahma sāma prāṇaṃ vyānam mano vā cakṣur apānam āhuś śrotraṃ śrotriyā bahudhā vadantī ti |
1.45.d: तद् ध पृथुर् वैन्यो दिव्यान् व्रात्यान् पप्रच्छे इन्द्रम् उक्थम् ऋचम् उद्गीथम् आहुर् ब्रह्म साम प्राणं व्यानम् मनो वा चक्षुर् अपानम् आहुश् श्रोत्रं श्रोत्रिया बहुधा वदन्ती ति ।
1.45.e: Now Prthu Vainya inquired this of the divine mendicants: " They call Indra uktha, re, udgītha, brahman, sāman, breath, vydna, or they call [him] mind, eye, apdna, ear; the learned speak [of him] in many ways."

1.45.s: te pratyūcur ṛṣaya ete mantrakṛtaḥ purājāḥ punar ājāyante vedānāṃ guptyai kam te vai vidvāṃso vainya tad vadanti samānam puruṣam bahudhā niviṣṭam iti |
1.45.d: ते प्रत्यूचुर् ऋषय एते मन्त्रकृतः पुराजाः पुनर् आजायन्ते वेदानां गुप्त्यै कम् ते वै विद्वांसो वैन्य तद् वदन्ति समानम् पुरुषम् बहुधा निविष्टम् इति ।
1.45.e: They answered: "These hymncomposing sages of old are born hither again for the keeping of the Vedas; verily they knowing [it], O Vainya, say this, that one and the same person is entered into many places."
1.45.m:
They answered:
'These ancient-born ṛṣis, makers of mantras, are born again for the sake of guarding the Vedas.
They, O Vainya, knowing that, speak of the same Person entered in many ways.'

1.45.s: imāṃ ha vā tad devatāṃ trayyāṃ vidyāyām imāṃ samānām abhy eka āpayanti naike yo ha vāvaitad evaṃ veda sa evaitāṃ devatāṃ samprati veda |
1.45.d: इमां ह वा तद् देवतां त्रय्यां विद्यायाम् इमां समानाम् अभ्य् एक आपयन्ति नैके यो ह वावैतद् एवं वेद स एवैतां देवतां सम्प्रति वेद ।
1.45.e: So some cause the attainment in the threefold knowledge of this divinity, this same one, others do not.
1.45.m: Some bring this deity to unity in the threefold knowledge, and some do not. He who knows this thus, he alone truly knows this deity.

1.45.s: sa eṣa indra udgīthaḥ sa yadaiṣa indra udgītha āgacchati naivodgātuś copagātṝṇāṃ ca vijñāyate ita evordhvas svar udeti sa upari mūrdhno lelāyati |
1.45.d: स एष इन्द्र उद्गीथः स यदैष इन्द्र उद्गीथ आगच्छति नैवोद्गातुश् चोपगातॄणां च विज्ञायते इत एवोर्ध्वस् स्वर् उदेति स उपरि मूर्ध्नो लेलायति ।
1.45.e: Verily he who knows this thus, he thoroughly knows this divinity,
1.45.m: This Indra is the udgītha. When this Indra, the udgītha, arrives, neither the udgātṛ's nor the assistant chanters' [voice] is distinguished; rising upward from here, svaḥ goes up; it flickers above the head.

1.45.s: sa vidyād āgamad indro neha kaś cana pāpmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśekṣyata iti tasmin ha na kaś cana pāpmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśiṣyate |
1.45.d: स विद्याद् आगमद् इन्द्रो नेह कश् चन पाप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशेक्ष्यत इति तस्मिन् ह न कश् चन पाप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशिष्यते ।
1.45.e: That same Indra is the udgitha. When this same Indra comes as udgītha, he is not distinguished both of the udgdtar and the upagdtars. He rises upward from here to heaven; he twinkles above the head.
1.45.m: He should know: "Indra has arrived; no evil inserted syllable will remain here." Indeed, no evil inserted syllable remains in him.

1.45.s: tad etad abhrātṛvyaṃ sāma na ha vā indraḥ kaṃ cana bhrātṛvyam paśyate sa yathendro na kaṃ cana bhrātṛvyam paśyata evam eva na kaṃ cana bhrātṛvyam paśyate ya etad evaṃ vedātho yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati | caturdaśe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ caturdaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
1.45.d: तद् एतद् अभ्रातृव्यं साम न ह वा इन्द्रः कं चन भ्रातृव्यम् पश्यते स यथेन्द्रो न कं चन भ्रातृव्यम् पश्यत एवम् एव न कं चन भ्रातृव्यम् पश्यते य एतद् एवं वेदाथो यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति । चतुर्दशे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः चतुर्दशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
1.45.e: He should know: " Indra hath come; no evil whatever, [not a] trace, will be left here;" truly in him no evil whatever, [not a] trace, is left. 7. That is the rivalless sāman. Verily Indra sees no rival whatever. As Indra sees no rival whatever, so he also sees no rival whatever who knows this thus, and also he for whom one knowing thus sings the udgītha.
1.45.m:
That is this sāman without a rival. Indra sees no rival at all. Just as Indra sees no rival, so one who knows this thus sees no rival at all; and likewise [he does not] for whom one who knows thus sings the udgītha.
Fourth khaṇḍa in the fourteenth anuvāka.
The fourteenth anuvāka is completed.

1.46.s: prajāpatir vā veda agra āsīt so 'kāmayata bahus syām prajāyeya bhūmānaṃ gaccheyam iti |
1.46.d: प्रजापतिर् वा वेद अग्र आसीत् सो ऽकामयत बहुस् स्याम् प्रजायेय भूमानं गच्छेयम् इति ।
1.46.e: Prajapati in the beginning was the Veda. He desired: " May I be many, may I beget progeny, may I attain manifoldness."
1.46.m: Prajāpati, truly, was this [universe] in the beginning. He desired: "May I be many; may I reproduce; may I attain abundance."

1.46.s: sa ṣoḍaśadhātmānaṃ vyakuruta bhadraṃ ca samāptiś cābhūtiś ca sambhūtiś ca bhūtaṃ ca sarvaṃ ca rūpaṃ cāparimitaṃ ca śrīś ca yaśaś ca nāma cāgraṃ ca sajātāś ca payaś ca mahīyā ca rasaś ca |
1.46.d: स षोडशधात्मानं व्यकुरुत भद्रं च समाप्तिश् चाभूतिश् च सम्भूतिश् च भूतं च सर्वं च रूपं चापरिमितं च श्रीश् च यशश् च नाम चाग्रं च सजाताश् च पयश् च महीया च रसश् च ।
1.46.e: He divided himself into sixteen parts: bliss and attainment and energy and growth and existence and the all and form and the infinite and fortune and glory and name and the summit and the fellows and milk and exaltation and sap.
1.46.m: He modified himself sixteenfold: the auspicious, completion, power to become, becoming, being, the all, form, the limitless, prosperity, fame, name, the summit, kin, milk, greatness, and essence.

1.46.s: tad yad bhadraṃ hṛdayam asya tat tatas saṃvatsaram asṛjata tad asya saṃvatsaro 'nūpatiṣṭhate |
1.46.d: तद् यद् भद्रं हृदयम् अस्य तत् ततस् संवत्सरम् असृजत तद् अस्य संवत्सरो ऽनूपतिष्ठते ।
1.46.e: What bliss is, that is his heart. Thence he created the year. That of him the year attends upon.
1.46.m: Now, that which is the auspicious, that is his heart. From that he created the year. The year attends upon that of his.

1.46.s: samāptiḥ karmāsya tat karmaṇā hi samāpnoti tata ṛtūn asṛjata tad asya rtavo 'nūpatiṣṭhante |
1.46.d: समाप्तिः कर्मास्य तत् कर्मणा हि समाप्नोति तत ऋतून् असृजत तद् अस्य र्तवो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते ।
1.46.e: Attainment, that is his action. For by action one attains. Thence he created the seasons. That of him the seasons attend upon.
1.46.m: Completion, that is his action. For through action one completes [a task]. From that he created the seasons. The seasons attend upon that of his.

1.46.s: ābhūtir annam asya tat caturdhā bhavati tato māsān ardhamāsān ahorātrāṇy uṣaso 'sṛjata tad asya māsā ardhamāsā ahorātrāṇy uṣaso 'nūpatiṣṭhante |
1.46.d: आभूतिर् अन्नम् अस्य तत् चतुर्धा भवति ततो मासान् अर्धमासान् अहोरात्राण्य् उषसो ऽसृजत तद् अस्य मासा अर्धमासा अहोरात्राण्य् उषसो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते ।
1.46.e: Energy, that is his food; that becomes four-fold. Thence he created months, half-months, nights and days, dawns. That of him months, halfmonths, nights and days, dawns attend upon.
1.46.m: Power to become, that is his food. It becomes fourfold. From that he created the months, the half-months, the days and nights, and the dawns. The months, the half-months, the days and nights, and the dawns attend upon that of his.

1.46.s: sambhūtī reto 'sya tad retaso hi sambhavati | pañcadaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.46.d: सम्भूती रेतो ऽस्य तद् रेतसो हि सम्भवति । पञ्चदशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
1.46.e: Growth, that is his seed. For from seed one grows.
1.46.m:
Becoming, that is his semen. For from semen one comes into being.
First khaṇḍa in the fifteenth anuvāka.

1.47.s: tataś candramasam asṛjata tad asya candramā anūpatiṣṭhate tasmāt sa retasaḥ pratirūpaḥ |
1.47.d: ततश् चन्द्रमसम् असृजत तद् अस्य चन्द्रमा अनूपतिष्ठते तस्मात् स रेतसः प्रतिरूपः ।
1.47.e: Thence he created the moon. That of him the moon attends upon. Therefore one corresponds to the seed.
1.47.m: From that he created the Moon. The Moon attends upon that of his. Therefore it is the counterpart of semen.

1.47.s: bhūtam prāṇo 'sya saḥ tato vāyum asṛjata tad asya vāyur anūpatiṣṭhate |
1.47.d: भूतम् प्राणो ऽस्य सः ततो वायुम् असृजत तद् अस्य वायुर् अनूपतिष्ठते ।
1.47.e: Existence, that is his breath. Thence he created the wind. That of him the wind attends upon.
1.47.m: Being, that is his breath. From that he created Vāyu. Vāyu attends upon that of his.

1.47.s: sarvam apāno 'sya saḥ tataḥ paśūn asṛjata tad asya paśavo 'nūpatiṣṭhante |
1.47.d: सर्वम् अपानो ऽस्य सः ततः पशून् असृजत तद् अस्य पशवो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते ।
1.47.e: The all, that is his apdna. Thence he created the domestic animals. That of him the domestic animals attend upon.
1.47.m: The all, that is his out-breath. From that he created beasts. Beasts attend upon that of his.

1.47.s: rūpaṃ vyāno 'sya saḥ tataḥ prajā asṛjata tad asya prajā anūpatiṣṭhante tasmād āsu prajāsu rūpāṇy adhigamyante |
1.47.d: रूपं व्यानो ऽस्य सः ततः प्रजा असृजत तद् अस्य प्रजा अनूपतिष्ठन्ते तस्माद् आसु प्रजासु रूपाण्य् अधिगम्यन्ते ।
1.47.e: Form, that is his vydna. Thence he created offspring. That of him offspring attends upon. Therefore among this offspring forms are found.
1.47.m: Form, that is his diffused breath. From that he created creatures. Creatures attend upon that of his. Therefore forms are perceived among these creatures.

1.47.s: aparimitam mano 'sya tat tato diśo 'sṛjata tad asya diśo 'nūpatiṣṭhante tasmāt tā aparimitāḥ aparimitam iva hi manaḥ |
1.47.d: अपरिमितम् मनो ऽस्य तत् ततो दिशो ऽसृजत तद् अस्य दिशो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते तस्मात् ता अपरिमिताः अपरिमितम् इव हि मनः ।
1.47.e: The infinite, that is his mind. Thence he created the quarters. That of him the quarters attend upon. Therefoi'e they are infinite; for infinite, as it were, is mind.
1.47.m: The limitless, that is his mind. From that he created the quarters. The quarters attend upon that of his. Therefore they are limitless, for the mind is, as it were, limitless.

1.47.s: śrīr vāg asya sā tatas samudram asṛjata tad asya samudro 'nūpatiṣṭhate |
1.47.d: श्रीर् वाग् अस्य सा ततस् समुद्रम् असृजत तद् अस्य समुद्रो ऽनूपतिष्ठते ।
1.47.e: Fortune, that is his speech. Thence he created the ocean. That of him the ocean attends upon.
1.47.m: Prosperity, that is his speech. From that he created the ocean. The ocean attends upon that of his.

1.47.s: yaśas tapo 'sya tat tato 'gnim asṛjata tad asyāgnir anūpatiṣṭhate tasmāt sa mathitād iva saṃtaptād iva jāyate |
1.47.d: यशस् तपो ऽस्य तत् ततो ऽग्निम् असृजत तद् अस्याग्निर् अनूपतिष्ठते तस्मात् स मथिताद् इव संतप्ताद् इव जायते ।
1.47.e: Grlory, that is his heat (penance). Thence he created fire. That of him the fire attends upon. Therefore it is born from the churned, as it were, from the thoroughly heated, as it were.
1.47.m: Fame, that is his ascetic heat. From that he created Agni. Agni attends upon that of his. Therefore it is born as if churned out, as if heated through.

1.47.s: nāma cakṣur asya tat | pañcadaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.47.d: नाम चक्षुर् अस्य तत् । पञ्चदशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
1.47.m:
Name, that is his sight.
Second khaṇḍa in the fifteenth anuvāka.

1.48.d: तत आदित्यम् असृजत तद् अस्यादित्यो ऽनूपतिष्ठते ।
1.48.e: Thence he created the sun That of him the sun attends upon.
1.48.m: From that he created Āditya. Āditya attends upon that of his.

1.48.s: agram mūrdhāsya saḥ tato divam asṛjata tad asya dyaur anūpatiṣṭhate |
1.48.d: अग्रम् मूर्धास्य सः ततो दिवम् असृजत तद् अस्य द्यौर् अनूपतिष्ठते ।
1.48.e: The summit, that is his head. Thence he created the sky. That of him the sky attends upon.
1.48.m: The summit, that is his head. From that he created heaven. Heaven attends upon that of his.

1.48.s: sajātā aṅgāny asya tāni aṅgair hi saha jāyate tato vanaspatīn asṛjata tad asya vanaspatayo 'nūpatiṣṭhante |
1.48.d: सजाता अङ्गान्य् अस्य तानि अङ्गैर् हि सह जायते ततो वनस्पतीन् असृजत तद् अस्य वनस्पतयो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते ।
1.48.e: The fellows, those are his limbs. For with his limbs one is born. Thence he created the forest-trees. That of him the forest-trees attend upon.
1.48.m: Kin, those are his limbs. For one is born together with limbs. From that he created the trees of the forest. The trees of the forest attend upon that of his.

1.48.s: payo lomāny asya tāni tata oṣadhīr asṛjata tad asyauṣadhayo 'nūpatiṣṭhante |
1.48.d: पयो लोमान्य् अस्य तानि तत ओषधीर् असृजत तद् अस्यौषधयो ऽनूपतिष्ठन्ते ।
1.48.e: Milk, that is the hair of his body. Thence he created the herbs. That of him the herbs attend upon.
1.48.m: Milk, that is his body-hairs. From that he created the plants. The plants attend upon that of his.

1.48.s: mahīyā māṃsāny asya tāni māṃsair hi saha mahīyate tato vayāṃsy asṛjata tad asya vayāṃsy anūpatiṣṭhante tasmāt tāni prapatiṣṇūni prapatiṣṇūnīva mahāmāṃsāni |
1.48.d: महीया मांसान्य् अस्य तानि मांसैर् हि सह महीयते ततो वयांस्य् असृजत तद् अस्य वयांस्य् अनूपतिष्ठन्ते तस्मात् तानि प्रपतिष्णूनि प्रपतिष्णूनीव महामांसानि ।
1.48.e: Exaltation, that is his flesh. For with the flesh one is exalted (?). Thence he created the birds. That of him the birds attend upon. Therefore they fly forth. Forth-flying (elastic?) as it were are the large [pieces of] flesh (?).
1.48.m: Greatness, that is his flesh. For through flesh one thrives. From that he created birds. Birds attend upon that of his. Therefore they fly forth; great pieces of flesh, as it were, fly forth.

1.48.s: raso majjāsya saḥ tataḥ pṛthivīm asṛjata tad asya pṛthivy anūpatiṣṭhate |
1.48.d: रसो मज्जास्य सः ततः पृथिवीम् असृजत तद् अस्य पृथिव्य् अनूपतिष्ठते ।
1.48.e: The sap, that is his marrow. Thence he created the earth. That of him the earth attends upon.
1.48.m: Essence, that is his marrow. From that he created the earth. The earth attends upon that of his.

1.48.s: sa haivaṃ ṣoḍaśadhātmānaṃ vikṛtya sārdhaṃ samait tad yat sārdhaṃ samaitat tat sāmnas sāmatvam |
1.48.d: स हैवं षोडशधात्मानं विकृत्य सार्धं समैत् तद् यत् सार्धं समैतत् तत् साम्नस् सामत्वम् ।
1.48.e: He thus having divided himself into sixteen parts came together. Because he came together (Wi + sam), that is the reason why the sdmaii is called so.
1.48.m: Having thus modified himself sixteenfold, he came together. In that he came together, that is the sāman-nature of the sāman.

1.48.s: sa evaiṣa hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣa udatiṣṭhat prajānāṃ janitā | pañcadaśe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.48.d: स एवैष हिरण्मयः पुरुष उदतिष्ठत् प्रजानां जनिता । पञ्चदशे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
1.48.e: That same one arose, a golden person, a generator of offspring.
1.48.m:
That very golden person arose, the begetter of creatures.
Third khaṇḍa in the fifteenth anuvāka.

1.49.s: devāsurā aspardhanta te devāḥ prajāpatim upādhāvañ jayāmāsurān iti |
1.49.d: देवासुरा अस्पर्धन्त ते देवाः प्रजापतिम् उपाधावञ् जयामासुरान् इति ।
1.49.e: The gods and the Asuras contended. These gods ran unto Prajapati [for help, saying]: " Let us overcome the Asuras."
1.49.m: The gods and the Asuras contended. Those gods ran to Prajāpati [saying]: "May we conquer the Asuras!"

1.49.s: so 'bravīn na vai māṃ yūyaṃ vittha nāsurāḥ yad vai māṃ yūyaṃ vidyāta tato vai yūyam eva syāta parāsurā bhaveyur iti |
1.49.d: सो ऽब्रवीन् न वै मां यूयं वित्थ नासुराः यद् वै मां यूयं विद्यात ततो वै यूयम् एव स्यात परासुरा भवेयुर् इति ।
1.49.e: He said; " Verily you do not know me, neither do the Asuras. Verily if you should know, then you would prevail, the Asuras would perish."
1.49.m: He said: "You do not know me, nor do the Asuras. If you were to know me, then you alone would be [victorious], and the Asuras would be defeated."

1.49.s: tad vai brūhīty abruvan so 'bravīt puruṣaḥ prajāpatis sāmeti mopāddhvam tato vai yūyam eva bhaviṣyatha parāsurā bhaviṣyantīti |
1.49.d: तद् वै ब्रूहीत्य् अब्रुवन् सो ऽब्रवीत् पुरुषः प्रजापतिस् सामेति मोपाद्ध्वम् ततो वै यूयम् एव भविष्यथ परासुरा भविष्यन्तीति ।
1.49.e: "Tell that," they said. He said: " Worship me [saying]: ' Purusa, Prajapati, Saraan.' Verily you will then prevail, the Asuras will perish."
1.49.m: They said: "Tell that to us!" He said: "Revere me as: 'The person, Prajāpati, is the sāman.' Then you alone will be [victorious], and the Asuras will be defeated."

1.49.s: tam puruṣaḥ prajāpatis sāmety upāsata tato vai devā abhavan parāsurāḥ sa yo haivaṃ vidvān puruṣaḥ prajāpatis sāmety upāste bhavaty ātmanā parāsya dviṣan bhrātṛvyo bhavati | pañcadaśe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ pañcadaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
1.49.d: तम् पुरुषः प्रजापतिस् सामेत्य् उपासत ततो वै देवा अभवन् परासुराः स यो हैवं विद्वान् पुरुषः प्रजापतिस् सामेत्य् उपास्ते भवत्य् आत्मना परास्य द्विषन् भ्रातृव्यो भवति । पञ्चदशे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः पञ्चदशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
1.49.e: They worshiped him [saying]: " Purusa, Prajapati, Saman." Thereupon the gods verily prevailed, the Asuras perished. He who knowing thus worships [saying]: " Purusa, Prajapati, Saman," prevails himself, his hostile rival perishes.
1.49.m:
They revered him as: "The person, Prajāpati, is the sāman." Thereupon the gods were [victorious], and the Asuras were defeated. He who, knowing thus, reveres [him] as: "The person, Prajāpati, is the sāman," thrives in himself, and his hating rival is defeated.
Fourth khaṇḍa in the fifteenth anuvāka.
The fifteenth anuvāka is completed.

1.50.s: devā vai vijigyānā abruvan dvitīyaṃ karavāmahai mādvitīyā bhūmeti te 'bruvan sāmaiva dvitīyaṃ karavāmahai sāmaiva no dvitīyam astv iti |
1.50.d: देवा वै विजिग्याना अब्रुवन् द्वितीयं करवामहै माद्वितीया भूमेति ते ऽब्रुवन् सामैव द्वितीयं करवामहै सामैव नो द्वितीयम् अस्त्व् इति ।
1.50.e: The gods, having completely conquered, said: "Let us make a second; let us not be without a second." They said: " Let us make the sdm,an the second; let the sdm,an be our second."
1.50.m: The gods, having been victorious, said: "Let us make a companion; let us not be without a companion." They said: "Let us make the sāman our companion; let the sāman be our companion!"

1.50.s: ta ime dyāvāpṛthivī abruvan sametaṃ sāma prajanayatam iti |
1.50.d: त इमे द्यावापृथिवी अब्रुवन् समेतं साम प्रजनयतम् इति ।
1.50.e: They said to this sky and earth: "Unite, bring forth the sāman." Yonder [sky] strongly abhorred this [earth]. He said: "Verily they do much on her of this kind and of that, they spit on her, they go about on her, they sit on her. Cleanse her now; verily she is unclean."
1.50.m: They said to these two, heaven and earth: "Come together; generate the sāman!"

1.50.s: so 'sāv asyā abībhatsata so 'bravīd bahu vā etasyāṃ kiṃ ca kiṃ ca kurvanty adhiṣṭhīvanty adhicaranty adhyāsate punīta nv enām apūtā vā iti |
1.50.d: सो ऽसाव् अस्या अबीभत्सत सो ऽब्रवीद् बहु वा एतस्यां किं च किं च कुर्वन्त्य् अधिष्ठीवन्त्य् अधिचरन्त्य् अध्यासते पुनीत न्व् एनाम् अपूता वा इति ।
1.50.e: They said to the gdthd: "With thee we will cleanse [her]." " What would be the consequence?" " Thou wouldst be gainer of a hundred." " Very well." They cleansed [her] with the gdthd. And therefore one obtains a hundred with the gdthd.
1.50.m: That one [heaven] felt disgust toward her [earth]. He said: "Indeed, much and various things do they do upon her: they spit upon her, they walk upon her, they sit upon her. Purify her first; she is indeed unpurified!"

1.50.s: te gāthām abruvan tvayā punāmeti kiṃ tatas syād iti śatasanis syā iti tatheti te gāthayāpunan tasmād uta gāthayā śataṃ sunoti |
1.50.d: ते गाथाम् अब्रुवन् त्वया पुनामेति किं ततस् स्याद् इति शतसनिस् स्या इति तथेति ते गाथयापुनन् तस्माद् उत गाथया शतं सुनोति ।
1.50.e: They said to the kumbyd: "With thee we will cleanse [her]." " What would be the consequence of it?" " Thou wouldst be gainer of a hundred." "Very well." They cleansed [her] with the Mimbyd. And therefore one obtains a hundred with the kumbyd.
1.50.m: They said to the Gāthā verse: "Let us purify [her] with you." "What would come of that?" [she asked]. "You will win a hundred," [they replied]. "So be it," [she said]. They purified [her] with the Gāthā verse. Therefore one also wins a hundred with a Gāthā verse.

1.50.s: te kumbyām abruvan tvayā punāmeti kiṃ tatas syād iti śatasanis syā iti tatheti te kumbyayāpunan tasmād uta kumbyayā śataṃ sunoti |
1.50.d: ते कुम्ब्याम् अब्रुवन् त्वया पुनामेति किं ततस् स्याद् इति शतसनिस् स्या इति तथेति ते कुम्ब्ययापुनन् तस्माद् उत कुम्ब्यया शतं सुनोति ।
1.50.e: They said to the ndrdpansl: "With thee we will clean ee [her]." "What would be the consequence of it." " Thou wouldst be gainer of a hundred." "Very well." They cleansed [her] with the ndrdfansl. And therefore one obtains a hundred with the ndrd^iarisi.
1.50.m: They said to the Kumbyā verse: "Let us purify [her] with you." "What would come of that?" [she asked]. "You will win a hundred," [they replied]. "So be it," [she said]. They purified [her] with the Kumbyā verse. Therefore one also wins a hundred with a Kumbyā verse.

1.50.s: te nārāśaṃsīm abruvan tvaya punāmeti kiṃ tatas syād iti śatasanis syā iti tatheti te nārāśaṃsyāpunan tasmād uta nārāśaṃsyā śataṃ sunoti |
1.50.d: ते नाराशंसीम् अब्रुवन् त्वय पुनामेति किं ततस् स्याद् इति शतसनिस् स्या इति तथेति ते नाराशंस्यापुनन् तस्माद् उत नाराशंस्या शतं सुनोति ।
1.50.e: They said to the rdibhl: " With thee we will cleanse [her]." " What would be the consequence of it?" "Thou wouldst be gainer of a hundred." " Very well." They cleansed [her] with the rdibhl. And therefore one obtains a hundred with the rdibhl.
1.50.m: They said to the Nārāśaṃsī verse: "Let us purify [her] with you." "What would come of that?" [she asked]. "You will win a hundred," [they replied]. "So be it," [she said]. They purified [her] with the Nārāśaṃsī verse. Therefore one also wins a hundred with a Nārāśaṃsī verse.

1.50.s: te raibhīm abruvan tvayā punāmeti kiṃ tatas syād iti śatasanis syā iti tatheti te raibhyāpunan tasmād uta raibhyā śataṃ sunoti |
1.50.d: ते रैभीम् अब्रुवन् त्वया पुनामेति किं ततस् स्याद् इति शतसनिस् स्या इति तथेति ते रैभ्यापुनन् तस्माद् उत रैभ्या शतं सुनोति ।
1.50.e: This [earth] here [was] cleansed. Then she said to yonder [sky]: "Verily much does a man practice of this sort and of that; cleanse thyself also."
1.50.m: They said to the Raibhī verse: "Let us purify [her] with you." "What would come of that?" [she asked]. "You will win a hundred," [they replied]. "So be it," [she said]. They purified [her] with the Raibhī verse. Therefore one also wins a hundred with a Raibhī verse.

1.50.s: seyam pūtā athāmum abravīd bahu vai kiṃ ca kiṃ ca pumāṃś carati tvam anupunīṣveti | ṣoḍaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.50.d: सेयम् पूता अथामुम् अब्रवीद् बहु वै किं च किं च पुमांश् चरति त्वम् अनुपुनीष्वेति । षोडशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
1.50.m:
She was purified. Then she said to that one [heaven]: "Indeed, much and various things does a male do. Purify yourself in return!"
First khaṇḍa in the sixteenth anuvāka.

1.51.s: sa ailabenāpunīta pūtāni ha vā asya sāmāni pūtā ṛcaḥ pūtāni yajūṃsi pūtam anūktam pūtaṃ sarvam bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
1.51.d: स ऐलबेनापुनीत पूतानि ह वा अस्य सामानि पूता ऋचः पूतानि यजूंसि पूतम् अनूक्तम् पूतं सर्वम् भवति य एवं वेद ।
1.51.e: He cleansed himself with noise (?). Verily the sāmans are cleansed, the ṛc's are cleansed, the yajuses are cleansed, the aniXkta is cleansed, the all is cleansed of him who knows thus.
1.51.m: He purified himself with the Ailaba verse. Purified indeed are the sāmans, purified the ṛcs, purified the yajuses, purified the recitation, purified is everything for him who knows thus.

1.51.s: te sametya sāma prājanayatām tad yat sametya sāma prājanayatāṃ tat sāmnas sāmatvam |
1.51.d: ते समेत्य साम प्राजनयताम् तद् यत् समेत्य साम प्राजनयतां तत् साम्नस् सामत्वम् ।
1.51.e: These two having united generated the sāman. Because they having united (^/i + sam) generated the sāman, therefore the sāman is called so.
1.51.m: The two, having come together, generated the sāman. In that they, having come together, generated the sāman, that is the sāman-nature of the sāman.

1.51.s: tad idaṃ sāma sṛṣṭam ada utkramya lelāyad atiṣṭhat tasya sarve devā mamatvina āsan mama mameti |
1.51.d: तद् इदं साम सृष्टम् अद उत्क्रम्य लेलायद् अतिष्ठत् तस्य सर्वे देवा ममत्विन आसन् मम ममेति ।
1.51.e: This same sāman, having been created, coming up there stood twinkling. All the gods were desirous of possessing it [saying]: " [It is] mine, [it is] mine."
1.51.m: This sāman, once created, went up yonder and stood trembling. All the gods claimed it as theirs, saying: "Mine, mine!"

1.51.s: te 'bruvan vīdam bhajāmahā iti tasya vibhāge na samapādayan tān prajāpatir abravīd apeta mama vā etat aham eva vo vibhakṣyāmīti |
1.51.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् वीदम् भजामहा इति तस्य विभागे न समपादयन् तान् प्रजापतिर् अब्रवीद् अपेत मम वा एतत् अहम् एव वो विभक्ष्यामीति ।
1.51.e: They said: " Let us share it out among ourselves." They did not agree in its division. Prajapati said to them: " Go away! Verily, this is mine. I will share it out among you."
1.51.m: They said: "Let us divide this among ourselves." They could not agree on its division. Prajāpati said to them: "Go away! This is mine. I myself will divide it for you."

1.51.s: so 'gnim abravīt tvaṃ vai me jyeṣṭhaḥ putrāṇām asi tvam prathamo vṛṇīṣveti |
1.51.d: सो ऽग्निम् अब्रवीत् त्वं वै मे ज्येष्ठः पुत्राणाम् असि त्वम् प्रथमो वृणीष्वेति ।
1.51.e: He said to Agni: "Verily, thou art the eldest of my sons; choose thou first."
1.51.m: He said to Agni: 'You are indeed the eldest of my sons. Choose first!'

1.51.s: so 'bravīn mandraṃ sāmno vṛṇe 'nnādyam iti sa ya etad gāyād annāda eva so 'san mām u sa devānām ṛcchād ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam etad gāyantam upavadād iti |
1.51.d: सो ऽब्रवीन् मन्द्रं साम्नो वृणे ऽन्नाद्यम् इति स य एतद् गायाद् अन्नाद एव सो ऽसन् माम् उ स देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एवं विद्वांसम् एतद् गायन्तम् उपवदाद् इति ।
1.51.e: He (A.) said: " I choose the soft (piano) of the sāman, i. e. the food-eating. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be a food-eater; and may he encounter me of the gods who speaketh ill of one who knowetli thus, who singeth this."
1.51.m: He said: 'I choose the deep-sounding [tone] of the sāman, [which is] food-eating. Whosoever sings this will surely become an eater of food; and whosoever censures him who knows thus as he sings this, will run up against me among the gods.'

1.51.e: Then he (P.) said to Indra: " Choose thou after [him]."
1.51.m: Then he said to Indra: 'You choose next!'

1.51.s: so 'bravīd ugraṃ sāmno vṛṇe śriyam iti sa ya etad gāyāc chrīmān eva so 'san mām u sa devānām ṛcchād ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam etad gāyantam upavadād iti |
1.51.d: सो ऽब्रवीद् उग्रं साम्नो वृणे श्रियम् इति स य एतद् गायाच् छ्रीमान् एव सो ऽसन् माम् उ स देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एवं विद्वांसम् एतद् गायन्तम् उपवदाद् इति ।
1.51.e: He (I.) said: "I choose the strong of the sāman, i. e. fortune. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be fortunate; and may he encounter me of the gods who speaketh ill of one who knoweth thus, who singeth this.
1.51.m: He said: 'I choose the powerful [tone] of the sāman, [which is] glory. Whosoever sings this will surely be glorious; and whosoever censures him who knows thus as he sings this, will run up against me among the gods.'

1.51.e: Then he said to Soma: " Choose thou after [him]."
1.51.m: Then he said to Soma: 'You choose next!'

1.51.s: so 'bravīd valgu sāmno vṛṇe priyam iti sa ya etad gāyāt priya eva sa kīrteḥ priyaś cakṣuṣaḥ priyas sarveṣām asan mām u sa devānām ṛcchād ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam etad gāyantam upavadād iti |
1.51.d: सो ऽब्रवीद् वल्गु साम्नो वृणे प्रियम् इति स य एतद् गायात् प्रिय एव स कीर्तेः प्रियश् चक्षुषः प्रियस् सर्वेषाम् असन् माम् उ स देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एवं विद्वांसम् एतद् गायन्तम् उपवदाद् इति ।
1.51.e: He (S.) said: " I choose the pleasant of the sāman, i. e. the dear. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be dear to fame, dear to sight, dear to all, and may he encounter me of the gods who speaketh ill of one who knoweth thus, who singeth this.
1.51.m: He said: 'I choose the sweet [tone] of the sāman, [which is] belovedness. Whosoever sings this will surely be beloved of fame, beloved of the eye, beloved of all; and whosoever censures him who knows thus as he sings this, will run up against me among the gods.'

1.51.e: Then he (P.) said to Brhaspati: " Choose thou after [him]." He (B.) said: " I choose the plover-like of the sāman, i. e. excellence in sacred lore. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be excellent in sacred lore; and may he encounter me of the gods who speaketh ill of one who knoweth thus, who singeth this."
1.51.m: Then he said to Bṛhaspati: 'You choose next!'

1.51.s: so 'bravīt krauñcaṃ sāmno vṛṇe brahmavarcasam iti sa ya etad gāyād brahmavarcasy eva so 'san mām u sa devānām ṛcchād ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam etad gāyantam upavadād iti | ṣoḍaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.51.d: सो ऽब्रवीत् क्रौञ्चं साम्नो वृणे ब्रह्मवर्चसम् इति स य एतद् गायाद् ब्रह्मवर्चस्य् एव सो ऽसन् माम् उ स देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एवं विद्वांसम् एतद् गायन्तम् उपवदाद् इति । षोडशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
1.51.m: He said: 'I choose the krauñca-tone of the sāman, [which is] brahmic lustre. Whosoever sings this will surely possess brahmic lustre; and whosoever censures him who knows thus as he sings this, will run up against me among the gods.' / The second khaṇḍa in the sixteenth anuvāka.

1.52.s: atha viśvān devān abravīd yūyam anuvṛṇīdhvam iti |
1.52.d: अथ विश्वान् देवान् अब्रवीद् यूयम् अनुवृणीध्वम् इति ।
1.52.e: Then he said to all the gods: " Choose ye after [himj."
1.52.m: Then he said to the All-gods: 'You choose next!'

1.52.s: te 'bruvan vaiśvadevaṃ sāmno vṛṇīmahe prajananam iti sa ya etad gāyāt prajāvān eva so 'sad asmān u devānām ṛcchād ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam etad gāyantam upavadād iti |
1.52.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् वैश्वदेवं साम्नो वृणीमहे प्रजननम् इति स य एतद् गायात् प्रजावान् एव सो ऽसद् अस्मान् उ देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एवं विद्वांसम् एतद् गायन्तम् उपवदाद् इति ।
1.52.e: They said: " We choose that of the sāman which belongs to all the gods, i. e. generation. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be rich in generation, and may he encounter us of the gods who speaketh ill of one who knoweth thus, who singeth this."
1.52.m: They said: 'We choose the Vaiśvadeva [tone] of the sāman, [which is] procreation. Whosoever sings this will surely have offspring; and whosoever censures him who knows thus as he sings this, will run up against us among the gods.'

1.52.s: atha paśūn abravīd yūyam anuvṛṇīdhvam iti |
1.52.d: अथ पशून् अब्रवीद् यूयम् अनुवृणीध्वम् इति ।
1.52.e: Then he said to the domestic animals: " Choose ye after [them]." They said: " Vayu is our lord; he will choose for us."
1.52.m: Then he said to the cattle: 'You choose next!'

1.52.s: te 'bruvan vāyur vā asmākam īśe sa eva no variṣyata iti te vāyuś ca paśavaś cābruvan niruktaṃ sāmno vṛṇīmahe paśavyam iti sa ya etad gāyāt paśumān eva so 'sad asmān u ca sa vāyuṃ ca devānām ṛcchād ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam etad gāyantam upavadād iti |
1.52.d: ते ऽब्रुवन् वायुर् वा अस्माकम् ईशे स एव नो वरिष्यत इति ते वायुश् च पशवश् चाब्रुवन् निरुक्तं साम्नो वृणीमहे पशव्यम् इति स य एतद् गायात् पशुमान् एव सो ऽसद् अस्मान् उ च स वायुं च देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एवं विद्वांसम् एतद् गायन्तम् उपवदाद् इति ।
1.52.e: They, Vfij'u and the domestic animals, said: " We choose the distinct [part] of the sāman, i. e. that which belongs to the domestic animals. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be rich in domestic animals; and may he encounter us and Vayu of the gods who speaketh ill of one who knoweth thus, who singeth this."
1.52.m: They said: 'Vāyu rules over us. He indeed will choose for us.' Vāyu and the cattle said: 'We choose the distinct [tone] of the sāman, [which is] rich in cattle. Whosoever sings this will surely have cattle; and whosoever censures him who knows thus as he sings this, will run up against us and against Vāyu among the gods.'

1.52.s: atha prajāpatir abravīd aham anuvariṣya iti |
1.52.d: अथ प्रजापतिर् अब्रवीद् अहम् अनुवरिष्य इति ।
1.52.e: Then Prajapati said: " I will choose after [them]."
1.52.m: Then Prajāpati said: 'I will choose next.'

1.52.s: so 'bravīd aniruktaṃ sāmno vṛṇe svargyam iti sa ya etad gāyāt svargaloka eva so 'san mām u sa devānām ṛcchād ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam etad gāyantam upavadād iti |
1.52.d: सो ऽब्रवीद् अनिरुक्तं साम्नो वृणे स्वर्ग्यम् इति स य एतद् गायात् स्वर्गलोक एव सो ऽसन् माम् उ स देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एवं विद्वांसम् एतद् गायन्तम् उपवदाद् इति ।
1.52.e: He said: " I choose the indistinct [part] of the sāman, i. e. that which belongs to heaven. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be in possession of the heavenly world, and may he encounter me of the gods who speaketh ill of one who knoweth thus, who singeth this.
1.52.m: He said: 'I choose the indistinct [tone] of the sāman, [which is] heavenly. Whosoever sings this will surely abide in the heavenly world; and whosoever censures him who knows thus as he sings this, will run up against me among the gods.'

1.52.e: Then he said to Varuna: " Choose thou after [me]."
1.52.m: Then he said to Varuṇa: 'You choose next!'

1.52.s: so 'bravīd yad vo na kaś canāvṛta tad aham parihariṣya iti kim iti apadhvāntaṃ sāmno vṛṇe 'paśavyam iti sa ya etad gāyād apaśur eva so 'san mām u sa devānām ṛcchād ya etad gāyād iti |
1.52.d: सो ऽब्रवीद् यद् वो न कश् चनावृत तद् अहम् परिहरिष्य इति किम् इति अपध्वान्तं साम्नो वृणे ऽपशव्यम् इति स य एतद् गायाद् अपशुर् एव सो ऽसन् माम् उ स देवानाम् ऋच्छाद् य एतद् गायाद् इति ।
1.52.e: He said: " What no one of you hath chosen, with that I will gird myself (?)." " What is it?" " I choose the ill-sonnding [part] of the sāman, i. e. that which does not belong to the domestic animals. Whosoever shall sing this, may he be without domestic animals, and may he encounter me of the gods who singeth this."
1.52.m: He said: 'Whatever of yours no one has chosen, that will I take over.' 'What [is that]?' 'I choose the muffled [tone] of the sāman, [which is] cattleless.' Whosoever sings this will surely be without cattle; and whosoever sings this will run up against me among the gods.

1.52.s: tāni vā etāny aṣṭau gītāgītāni sāmnaḥ imāny u ha vai sapta gītāni atheyam eva vāruṇy āgāgītā |
1.52.d: तानि वा एतान्य् अष्टौ गीतागीतानि साम्नः इमान्य् उ ह वै सप्त गीतानि अथेयम् एव वारुण्य् आगागीता ।
1.52.e: These same then are eight [«Śa«] of the sāman, sung and unsung; and verily these seven are sung, but this dgd belonging to Varuna is not sung.
1.52.m: These are indeed the eight chanted and unchanted [modes] of the sāman. These seven are indeed to be chanted; but this chant of Varuṇa is not to be chanted.

1.52.s: sa yāṃ ha kāṃ caivaṃ vidvān etāsāṃ saptānām āgānāṃ gāyati gītam evāsya bhavaty etān u kāmān rādhnoti ya etāsu kāmāḥ athemām eva vāruṇīm āgāṃ na gāyet | ṣoḍaśe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ ṣoḍaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
1.52.d: स यां ह कां चैवं विद्वान् एतासां सप्तानाम् आगानां गायति गीतम् एवास्य भवत्य् एतान् उ कामान् राध्नोति य एतासु कामाः अथेमाम् एव वारुणीम् आगां न गायेत् । षोडशे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः षोडशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
1.52.e: Whichever of these seven dgds any one knowing thus sings, of him [the sāman?\ is sung, and he accomplishes those wishes which are in these \dgds\ And this dgd belonging to Varuna one should not sing.
1.52.m: Whichever of these seven chants one sings, knowing thus, it becomes truly chanted for him, and he attains those desires which are in them. But this chant of Varuṇa he should not sing. / The third khaṇḍa in the sixteenth anuvāka. / The sixteenth anuvāka is ended.

1.53.s: dvayaṃ vāvedam agra āsīt sac caivāsac ca |
1.53.d: द्वयं वावेदम् अग्र आसीत् सच् चैवासच् च ।
1.53.e: Verily, this [all] was twofold in the beginning: the existent and the non-existent.
1.53.m: In the beginning, this [universe] was indeed twofold: the real and the unreal.

1.53.s: tayor yat sat tat sāma tan manas sa prāṇaḥ atha yad asat sa rk sā vāk so 'pānaḥ |
1.53.d: तयोर् यत् सत् तत् साम तन् मनस् स प्राणः अथ यद् असत् स र्क् सा वाक् सो ऽपानः ।
1.53.e: Of these two the existent, that is the sāman, the mind, breath; and the non-existent, that is the re, speech, exhalation. That which is mind and breath, that is the same; and that which is speech and exhalation, that is the same. This resting-place is mind and breath; this resting-place is speech and exhalation. Therefore a man lies by a woman at the right side.
1.53.m: Of the two, that which is the real is the sāman, it is the mind, it is the out-breath; and that which is the unreal is the ṛc, it is speech, it is the in-breath.

1.53.s: tad yan manaś ca prāṇaś ca tat samānam atha yā vāk cāpānaś ca tat samānam idam āyatanam manaś ca prāṇaś cedam āyatanaṃ vāk cāpānaś ca tasmāt pumān dakṣiṇato yoṣām upaśete |
1.53.d: तद् यन् मनश् च प्राणश् च तत् समानम् अथ या वाक् चापानश् च तत् समानम् इदम् आयतनम् मनश् च प्राणश् चेदम् आयतनं वाक् चापानश् च तस्मात् पुमान् दक्षिणतो योषाम् उपशेते ।
1.53.m: Then that which is mind and out-breath, that is the same; and that which is speech and in-breath, that is the same. Mind and out-breath are this abode, and speech and in-breath are this abode. Therefore a man lies down to the right of a woman.

1.53.s: seyam ṛg asmin sāman mithunam aicchata tām apṛcchat kā tvam asīti sāham asmīty abravīt atha vā aham amo 'smīti |
1.53.d: सेयम् ऋग् अस्मिन् सामन् मिथुनम् ऐच्छत ताम् अपृच्छत् का त्वम् असीति साहम् अस्मीत्य् अब्रवीत् अथ वा अहम् अमो ऽस्मीति ।
1.53.e: This tc desired intercourse with this sāman. He (the sāman) asked her (the re): " Who art thou?" She answered: "I am she (sd)." "Verily, then, I am he (ama)."
1.53.m: This ṛc desired union with this sāman. He asked her: 'Who are you?' She said: 'I am Sā (she).' 'Then I am indeed Ama (he).'

1.53.s: tad yat sā cāmaś ca tat sāmābhavat tat sāmnas sāmatvam |
1.53.d: तद् यत् सा चामश् च तत् सामाभवत् तत् साम्नस् सामत्वम् ।
1.53.e: What was she {sd.) and he {ama), that became the sdr/tan; that is the reason why the sāman is called so.
1.53.m: Because it was Sā and Ama, therefore it became sāman: that is the sāman-nature of the sāman.

1.53.s: tau vai sambhavāveti nety abravīt svasā vai mama tvam asy anyatra mithunam icchasveti |
1.53.d: तौ वै सम्भवावेति नेत्य् अब्रवीत् स्वसा वै मम त्वम् अस्य् अन्यत्र मिथुनम् इच्छस्वेति ।
1.53.e: " Let us two here have intercourse." " No," he said, " verily thou art my sister; desire intercourse elsewhere."
1.53.m: 'Let us two unite!' 'No,' he said, 'you are my sister. Seek a mate elsewhere!'

1.53.s: sābravīn na vai taṃ vindāmi yena sambhaveyam tvayaiva sambhavānīti sā vai punīṣvety abravīt apūtā vā asīti |
1.53.d: साब्रवीन् न वै तं विन्दामि येन सम्भवेयम् त्वयैव सम्भवानीति सा वै पुनीष्वेत्य् अब्रवीत् अपूता वा असीति ।
1.53.e: She said: "Verily, I find no one with whom I might have intercourse; let me have intercourse with thee." " Then cleanse thyself," he said; " verily thou art unclean."
1.53.m: She said: 'I find no one with whom I might unite. Let me unite with you alone.' 'Purify yourself then,' he said, 'for you are unpurified.'

1.53.s: sāpunīta yad idaṃ viprā vadanti tena sābravīt kvedam bhaviṣyatīti pratyūhety abravīt dhīr vā eṣā prajānāṃ jīvanaṃ vā etad bhaviṣyatīti tatheti tat pratyauhat tasmād eṣā dhīr eva prajānāṃ jīvanam eva |
1.53.d: सापुनीत यद् इदं विप्रा वदन्ति तेन साब्रवीत् क्वेदम् भविष्यतीति प्रत्यूहेत्य् अब्रवीत् धीर् वा एषा प्रजानां जीवनं वा एतद् भविष्यतीति तथेति तत् प्रत्यौहत् तस्माद् एषा धीर् एव प्रजानां जीवनम् एव ।
1.53.e: She cleansed herself with that which the inspired bards say. She said: " What is to become of this?" " Cast it back," he said; " verily this is device; it will become the living of people." " Yes." She cast it back. Therefore is this device the living of people.
1.53.m: She purified herself through that which the inspired poets speak here. She said: 'Where will this [impurified matter] go?' 'Push it away,' he said; 'this is inspired thought; this will become the livelihood of creatures.' 'So be it.' She pushed it away. Therefore this is inspired thought, this is indeed the livelihood of creatures.

1.53.s: punīṣvety abravīt sāpunīta gāthayā sāpunīta kumbyayā sāpunīta nārāśaṃsyā sāpunīta purāṇetihāsena sāpunīta yad idam ādāya nāgāyanti tena |
1.53.d: पुनीष्वेत्य् अब्रवीत् सापुनीत गाथया सापुनीत कुम्ब्यया सापुनीत नाराशंस्या सापुनीत पुराणेतिहासेन सापुनीत यद् इदम् आदाय नागायन्ति तेन ।
1.53.e: " Cleanse thyself," he said. She cleansed herself with the gdthd, she cleansed herself with the kumbyd, she cleansed herself with the ndrd^ansl, she cleansed herself with the purdna and itihdsa, she cleansed herself with that which they do not sing here when starting (?).
1.53.m: He said: 'Purify yourself!' She purified herself with the gāthā; she purified herself with the kumbyā; she purified herself with the nārāśaṃsī; she purified herself with the purāṇa and itihāsa; she purified herself with that taking which they do not sing here.

1.53.s: sābravīt kvedam bhaviṣyatīti pratyūhety abravīt dhīr vā eṣā prajānāṃ jīvanaṃ vā etad bhaviṣyatīti tatheti tat pratyauhat tasmād eṣā dhīr v eva prajānāṃ jīvanam v eva |
1.53.d: साब्रवीत् क्वेदम् भविष्यतीति प्रत्यूहेत्य् अब्रवीत् धीर् वा एषा प्रजानां जीवनं वा एतद् भविष्यतीति तथेति तत् प्रत्यौहत् तस्माद् एषा धीर् व् एव प्रजानां जीवनम् व् एव ।
1.53.e: She said: " What is to become of it?" " Cast it back," he said; " verily this is device. It will become the living of people." "Yes." She cast it back. Therefore this is both device and the living of people.
1.53.m: She said: 'Where will this [impurified matter] go?' 'Push it away,' he said; 'this is inspired thought; this will become the livelihood of creatures.' 'So be it.' She pushed it away. Therefore this is indeed inspired thought, this is indeed the livelihood of creatures.

1.53.d: पुनीष्वैवेत्य् अब्रवीत् । सप्तदशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
1.53.m: 'Purify yourself further!' he said. / The first khaṇḍa in the seventeenth anuvāka.

1.54.s: sā madhunāpunīta tasmād uta brahmacārī madhu nāśnīyād vedasya palāva iti kāmaṃ ha tv ācāryadattam aśnīyāt |
1.54.d: सा मधुनापुनीत तस्माद् उत ब्रह्मचारी मधु नाश्नीयाद् वेदस्य पलाव इति कामं ह त्व् आचार्यदत्तम् अश्नीयात् ।
1.54.e: She cleansed herself with honey. And therefore a Vedic student should not eat honey [saying]: " [It is] the husk of the Veda." But he may eat at pleasure what his teacher gives him.
1.54.m: She purified herself with honey. Therefore a Vedic student should not eat honey, [thinking:] 'It is the chaff of the Veda.' At will, however, he may eat what is given by his teacher.

1.54.s: atha rk sāmābravīd bahu vai kiṃ ca kiṃ ca pumāṃś carati tvam anupunīṣveti sa bharaṇḍakeṣṇenāpunīta pūtāni ha vā asya sāmāni pūtā ṛcaḥ pūtāni yajūṃṣi pūtam anūktam pūtaṃ sarvam bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
1.54.d: अथ र्क् सामाब्रवीद् बहु वै किं च किं च पुमांश् चरति त्वम् अनुपुनीष्वेति स भरण्डकेष्णेनापुनीत पूतानि ह वा अस्य सामानि पूता ऋचः पूतानि यजूंषि पूतम् अनूक्तम् पूतं सर्वम् भवति य एवं वेद ।
1.54.e: Now the re said to the sāman: " Verily much does a man practice of one sort and another; cleanse thyself also." He cleansed himself with = I. 51. i.
1.54.m: Then the ṛc said to the sāman: 'A man pursues much and manifold things. Purify yourself in turn!' He purified himself through bharaṇḍakeṣṇa. Purified indeed are his sāmans, purified his ṛcs, purified his yajuses, purified what is recited, purified is everything for him who knows thus.

1.54.s: tābhyāṃ sado mithunāya paryaśrayan tasmād upavasathīyāṃ rātriṃ sadasi na śayīta atra hy etāv ṛksāme upavasathīyāṃ rātriṃ sadasi sambhavataḥ sa yathā śreyasa upadraṣṭaivaṃ hi śaśvad īśvaro 'nulabdhaḥ parābhavitoḥ |
1.54.d: ताभ्यां सदो मिथुनाय पर्यश्रयन् तस्माद् उपवसथीयां रात्रिं सदसि न शयीत अत्र ह्य् एताव् ऋक्सामे उपवसथीयां रात्रिं सदसि सम्भवतः स यथा श्रेयस उपद्रष्टैवं हि शश्वद् ईश्वरो ऽनुलब्धः पराभवितोः ।
1.54.e: They enclosed the sadas for their intercourse. Therefore in the night of the fastday one should not lie in the sadas; for there, in the sadas, these two, re and sāman, have intercourse in the night of the fast-day. For, as one who spies upon a superior, even so he, apprehended, is altogether likely to perish.
1.54.m: For the two they enclosed the sadas for union. Therefore one should not sleep in the sadas on the upavasatha night, for here on the upavasatha night these two, ṛc and sāman, unite in the sadas. As one who spies on his superior, so indeed is he constantly liable to perish when caught.

1.54.s: atho āhur udgātur mukhe sambhavataḥ udgātur eva mukhaṃ nekṣeteti |
1.54.d: अथो आहुर् उद्गातुर् मुखे सम्भवतः उद्गातुर् एव मुखं नेक्षेतेति ।
1.54.e: Now they say: " In the mouth of the udgatar they have intercourse; one should not look at the mouth of the udgatar.''''
1.54.m: Moreover, they say: 'They unite in the mouth of the udgātṛ; one should not look at the face of the udgātṛ.'

1.54.s: tad u vā āhuḥ kāmam evodgātur mukham īkṣeta upavasathīyām evaitāṃ rātriṃ sadasi na śayīta atra hy evaitāv ṛksāme upavasathīyāṃ rātriṃ sadasi sambhavata iti |
1.54.d: तद् उ वा आहुः कामम् एवोद्गातुर् मुखम् ईक्षेत उपवसथीयाम् एवैतां रात्रिं सदसि न शयीत अत्र ह्य् एवैताव् ऋक्सामे उपवसथीयां रात्रिं सदसि सम्भवत इति ।
1.54.e: But they also say this: " He may look at pleasure at the mouth of the udgatar. Only in this night of the fast-day he should not lie in the sadas; for there, in the sadas, these two, re and sdm,an, have intercourse in the night of the fast-day."
1.54.m: Concerning this, however, they say: 'One may freely look at the face of the udgātṛ; only on this upavasatha night should one not sleep in the sadas, for here indeed on the upavasatha night these two, ṛc and sāman, unite in the sadas.'

1.54.s: tāṃ sambhaviṣyann āhāmo 'ham asmi sā tvaṃ sā tvam asy amo 'ham sā mām anuvratā bhūtvā prajāḥ prajanayāvahai ehi sambhavāvahā iti |
1.54.d: तां सम्भविष्यन्न् आहामो ऽहम् अस्मि सा त्वं सा त्वम् अस्य् अमो ऽहम् सा माम् अनुव्रता भूत्वा प्रजाः प्रजनयावहै एहि सम्भवावहा इति ।
1.54.e: When he was about to have intercourse with her, he said: " I am he, thou art she; thou art she, I am he; becoming obedient to me (my wife), let us generate offspring. Come! let us have intercourse."
1.54.m: Being about to unite with her, he said: 'Ama am I, Sā are you; Sā are you, Ama am I. Being devoted to me, let us two generate offspring! Come, let us unite!'

1.54.s: tāṃ sambhavann atyaricyata so 'bravīn na vai tvānubhavāmi virāḍ bhūtvā prajanayāreti tatheti |
1.54.d: तां सम्भवन्न् अत्यरिच्यत सो ऽब्रवीन् न वै त्वानुभवामि विराड् भूत्वा प्रजनयारेति तथेति ।
1.54.e: When he had intercourse with her, he exceeded. He said: " Verily, I am not adapted to thee. Having become the virdj let us two generate." " Yes."
1.54.m: Uniting with her, he exceeded [her]. He said: 'I do not fill you. Become the virāj and bring forth!' 'So be it.'

1.54.s: tau virāḍ bhūtvā prājanayatām hiṅkāraś cāhāvaś ca prastāvaś ca prathamā codgīthaś ca madhyamā ca pratihāraś cottamā ca nidhanaṃ ca vaṣaṭkāraś caivaṃ virāḍ bhūtvā prājanayatām te amum ajanayatāṃ yo 'sau tapati te vyadravatām | saptadaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.54.d: तौ विराड् भूत्वा प्राजनयताम् हिङ्कारश् चाहावश् च प्रस्तावश् च प्रथमा चोद्गीथश् च मध्यमा च प्रतिहारश् चोत्तमा च निधनं च वषट्कारश् चैवं विराड् भूत्वा प्राजनयताम् ते अमुम् अजनयतां यो ऽसौ तपति ते व्यद्रवताम् । सप्तदशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
1.54.e: They, having become the virdj, generated. [As] and middle \dgd?'\ and pratihāra and last [dgd .?] and nidhana and vasatJcdra—thus having become the virdj they brought forth. They generated him who burns yonder. They ran apart—
1.54.m: The two, having become the virāj, procreated: the hiṅkāra and the āhāva, the prastāva and the first [verse], the udgītha and the middle [verse], the pratihāra and the last [verse], the nidhana and the vaṣaṭ-call—thus having become the virāj, the two procreated. They two brought forth that one who burns yonder. They two ran apart. Second khaṇḍa in the seventeenth anuvāka.

1.55.s: mad adhy abhū3n mad adhy abhū3d iti tasmād āhur madhuputra iti |
1.55.d: मद् अध्य् अभू3न् मद् अध्य् अभू3द् इति तस्माद् आहुर् मधुपुत्र इति ।
1.55.e: I. 55. 1.—[saying]: "Hath he originated from me {mad adhy abhut)? Hath he originated from me?" Therefore they say "honey-son" (madhuputra). And therefore women do not eat honey, saying: " We perform this vow of sons."
1.55.m: "From me he has come into being! From me he has come into being!" [each said]. Therefore they say, "son of honey" (madhuputra).

1.55.s: tasmād uta striyo madhu nāśnanti putrāṇām idaṃ vrataṃ carāma iti vadantīḥ | tad ayaṃ tṛco 'nūdaśrayata iyam eva gāyatry antarikṣaṃ triṣṭub asau jagatī tasyaitat tṛcaḥ |
1.55.d: तस्माद् उत स्त्रियो मधु नाश्नन्ति पुत्राणाम् इदं व्रतं चराम इति वदन्तीः । तद् अयं तृचो ऽनूदश्रयत इयम् एव गायत्र्य् अन्तरिक्षं त्रिष्टुब् असौ जगती तस्यैतत् तृचः ।
1.55.e: Then this triplet rose up in consequence: this [earth] the gāyatrī; the atmosphere the tristubh; yonder [sky] the jagatt. That is its triplet.
1.55.m: Therefore also women do not eat honey, saying, "We are observing this vow for [our] sons." Then this triplet [of verses] arose following [them]: this [earth] is the gāyatrī, the intermediate space is the triṣṭubh, yonder [heaven] is the jagatī. Of him this is the triplet.

1.55.s: sa upariṣṭāt sāmādhyāhitaṃ tapati so 'dhruva ivāsīd alelāyad iva sa nordhvo 'tapat |
1.55.d: स उपरिष्टात् सामाध्याहितं तपति सो ऽध्रुव इवासीद् अलेलायद् इव स नोर्ध्वो ऽतपत् ।
1.55.e: He (yonder sun) burns on high, a sdm,an set above. He was unstable, as it were; he twinkled, as it were. He did not burn upward.
1.55.m: He, placed above the sāman, burns. He was as if unsteady, as if trembling. He did not burn upwards.

1.55.s: sa devān abravīd un mā gāyateti kiṃ tatas syād iti śriyaṃ vaḥ prayaccheyam mām iha dṛṃheteti |
1.55.d: स देवान् अब्रवीद् उन् मा गायतेति किं ततस् स्याद् इति श्रियं वः प्रयच्छेयम् माम् इह दृंहेतेति ।
1.55.e: He said to the gods: "Sing me iha udgitha.'''' " What would be the result?" " I would bestow fortune upon you. Make me firm here."
1.55.m: He said to the gods: "Sing up to me (un mā gāyata)." [They said:] "What would come of that?" [He said:] "I would grant you prosperity. Make me firm here!"

1.55.s: tatheti tam udagāyan tam etad atrādṛṃhan tebhyaś śriyam prāyacchat saiṣā devānāṃ śrīḥ |
1.55.d: तथेति तम् उदगायन् तम् एतद् अत्रादृंहन् तेभ्यश् श्रियम् प्रायच्छत् सैषा देवानां श्रीः ।
1.55.e: " Very well." They sang him the udgītha. They thus made him firm there. He bestowed fortune upon them. That is that fortune of the gods.
1.55.m: "So be it." They sang up to him (udagāyan). They made him firm here. He granted them prosperity. That is this prosperity of the gods.

1.55.s: tata etad ūrdhvas tapati sa nārvāṅ atapat |
1.55.d: तत एतद् ऊर्ध्वस् तपति स नार्वाङ् अतपत् ।
1.55.e: Hence he thus burns upwards. He did not burn hitherward.
1.55.m: Then he burns upwards. He did not burn downwards.

1.55.s: sa ṛṣīn abravīd anu mā gāyateti kiṃ tatas syād iti śriyaṃ vaḥ prayaccheyam mām iha dṛṃheteti |
1.55.d: स ऋषीन् अब्रवीद् अनु मा गायतेति किं ततस् स्याद् इति श्रियं वः प्रयच्छेयम् माम् इह दृंहेतेति ।
1.55.e: He said to the sages {rsi): " Sing after me." " What would be the result of it?" " I would bestow fortune upon you. Make me firm here."
1.55.m: He said to the ṛṣis: "Sing along to me (anu mā gāyata)." [They said:] "What would come of that?" [He said:] "I would grant you prosperity. Make me firm here!"

1.55.s: tatheti tam anvagāyan tam etad atrādṛṃhan tebhyaś śriyam prāyacchat saiṣa rṣīṇāṃ śrīḥ |
1.55.d: तथेति तम् अन्वगायन् तम् एतद् अत्रादृंहन् तेभ्यश् श्रियम् प्रायच्छत् सैष र्षीणां श्रीः ।
1.55.e: " Very well." They sang after him. They thus made him firm there. He bestowed fortune upon them. That is that fortune of the sages.
1.55.m: "So be it." They sang along to him (anvagāyan). They made him firm here. He granted them prosperity. That is this prosperity of the ṛṣis.

1.55.s: tata etad arvāṅ tapati sa na tiryaṅ atapat |
1.55.d: तत एतद् अर्वाङ् तपति स न तिर्यङ् अतपत् ।
1.55.e: Hence he thus burns hitherward. He did not burn crosswise.
1.55.m: Then he burns downwards. He did not burn transversely.

1.55.s: sa gandharvāpsaraso 'bravīd ā mā gāyateti kiṃ tatas syād iti śriyaṃ vaḥ prayaccheyam mām iha dṛṃheteti |
1.55.d: स गन्धर्वाप्सरसो ऽब्रवीद् आ मा गायतेति किं ततस् स्याद् इति श्रियं वः प्रयच्छेयम् माम् इह दृंहेतेति ।
1.55.e: He said to the Gandharvas and Apsarases: " Sing unto me." " What would be the result of it?" "I would bestow fortune upon you. Make me firm here."
1.55.m: He said to the Gandharvas and Apsarases: "Sing hither to me (ā mā gāyata)." [They said:] "What would come of that?" [He said:] "I would grant you prosperity. Make me firm here!"
