1.55.s: tatheti tam āgāyan tam etad atrādṛṃhan tebhyaś śriyam prāyacchat saiṣā gandharvāpsarasāṃ śrīḥ |
1.55.d: तथेति तम् आगायन् तम् एतद् अत्रादृंहन् तेभ्यश् श्रियम् प्रायच्छत् सैषा गन्धर्वाप्सरसां श्रीः ।
1.55.e: "Very well." They sang unto him. They thus made him firm there. He bestowed fortune upon them. That is that fortune of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.
1.55.m: "So be it." They sang hither to him (āgāyan). They made him firm here. He granted them prosperity. That is this prosperity of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.

1.55.s: tāni vā etāni trīṇi sāmna udgītam anugītam āgītam tad yathedaṃ vayam āgāyodgāyāma etad udgītam atha yad yathāgītaṃ tad anugītam atha yat kiṃ ceti sāmnas tad āgītam etāni hy eva trīṇi sāmnaḥ | saptadaśe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ saptadaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
1.55.d: तानि वा एतानि त्रीणि साम्न उद्गीतम् अनुगीतम् आगीतम् तद् यथेदं वयम् आगायोद्गायाम एतद् उद्गीतम् अथ यद् यथागीतं तद् अनुगीतम् अथ यत् किं चेति साम्नस् तद् आगीतम् एतानि ह्य् एव त्रीणि साम्नः । सप्तदशे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः सप्तदशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
1.55.e: Verily these are the three of the sāman [viz.]: what is sung as udgītha, what is sung after (amtglta), what is sung unto (dg'ita). As we here having sung unto sing the udgītha, that is what is sung as udgītha; and what is sung like the dglta, that is that which is sung after; and anything of the sāman [that is sung], that is sung unto. For there are just these three [parts] of the sāman.
1.55.m: These indeed are the three chantings of the sāman: the udgīta, the anugīta, and the āgīta. That which we sing hither and sing up, this is the udgīta. And that which is sung along, that is the anugīta. And whatever else of the sāman, that is the āgīta. For these are the three of the sāman. Third khaṇḍa in the seventeenth anuvāka. The seventeenth anuvāka is ended.

1.56.s: āpo vā idam agre mahat salilam āsīt sa ūrmir ūrmim askandat tato hiraṇmayau kukṣyau samabhavatāṃ te eva rksāme |
1.56.d: आपो वा इदम् अग्रे महत् सलिलम् आसीत् स ऊर्मिर् ऊर्मिम् अस्कन्दत् ततो हिरण्मयौ कुक्ष्यौ समभवतां ते एव र्क्सामे ।
1.56.e: This all was at first the waters, a great flood. One wave mounted [the other] wave. Thence two golden wombs came into being, these two [viz.]: re and sāman.
1.56.m: In the beginning, waters indeed were this great ocean. Wave leaped upon wave. Thence two golden halves of a shell came into being; they were indeed the ṛc and the sāman.

1.56.s: seyam ṛg idaṃ sāmābhyaplavata tām apṛcchat kā tvam asīti sāham asmīty abravīt atha vā aham amo 'smīti tad yat sā cāmaś ca tat sāmnas sāmatvam |
1.56.d: सेयम् ऋग् इदं सामाभ्यप्लवत ताम् अपृच्छत् का त्वम् असीति साहम् अस्मीत्य् अब्रवीत् अथ वा अहम् अमो ऽस्मीति तद् यत् सा चामश् च तत् साम्नस् सामत्वम् ।
1.56.e: This same re floated unto that same sāman. = I. 53. 6. 3. = I. 53. e.
1.56.m: This ṛc floated towards this sāman. He asked her: "Who are you?" She said: "I am she (sā)." [He said:] "Now, indeed, I am he (ama)." That she was sā and he ama, that is the sāman-hood of the sāman.

1.56.s: tau vai sambhavāveti nety abravīt svasā vai mama tvam asi anyatra mithunam icchasveti |
1.56.d: तौ वै सम्भवावेति नेत्य् अब्रवीत् स्वसा वै मम त्वम् असि अन्यत्र मिथुनम् इच्छस्वेति ।
1.56.m: "Let us two unite!" [said the sāman]. She said: "No, you are indeed my brother. Seek a mate elsewhere!"

1.56.s: sā parāplavata mithunam icchamānā sā samās sahasraṃ saptatīḥ paryaplavata |
1.56.d: सा पराप्लवत मिथुनम् इच्छमाना सा समास् सहस्रं सप्ततीः पर्यप्लवत ।
1.56.e: She floated away desiring intercourse. She floated around a thousand seventies of years,
1.56.m: She floated away, seeking a mate. She floated around for seventy thousand years.

1.56.s: tad eṣa ślokas strī smaivāgre saṃcaratīcchantī salile patim samās sahasraṃ saptatīs tato 'jāyata paśyata iti |
1.56.d: तद् एष श्लोकस् स्त्री स्मैवाग्रे संचरतीच्छन्ती सलिले पतिम् समास् सहस्रं सप्ततीस् ततो ऽजायत पश्यत इति ।
1.56.e: Regarding this there is this ŚloJea: " In the beginning the woman used to go seeking [her] lord in the flood, one thousand seventies of years; thence the beauteous one was born."

1.56.s: asau vā ādityaḥ paśyataḥ eṣa eva tad ajāyata etena hi paśyati |
1.56.d: असौ वा आदित्यः पश्यतः एष एव तद् अजायत एतेन हि पश्यति ।
1.56.e: Yonder sun is the beauteous one [pafyata); he was born then, for by him one sees {pa^yati).
1.56.m: Yonder sun is indeed the Seer. He indeed was born then, for by him one sees.

1.56.s: sāvittvā nyaplavata sābravīn na vai taṃ vindāmi yena sambhaveyam tvayaiva sambhavānīti |
1.56.d: सावित्त्वा न्यप्लवत साब्रवीन् न वै तं विन्दामि येन सम्भवेयम् त्वयैव सम्भवानीति ।
1.56.e: She, not having found [anyone], floated in. She said: "Verily I find no one with whom I might have intercourse. Let me have intercourse with thee."
1.56.m: Having found [none], she floated back down. She said: "Indeed, I find no one with whom I may unite. Let me unite with you alone!"

1.56.s: sā vai dvitīyām icchasvety abravīn na vai maikodyaṃsyasīti sā dvitīyāṃ vittvā nyaplavata |
1.56.d: सा वै द्वितीयाम् इच्छस्वेत्य् अब्रवीन् न वै मैकोद्यंस्यसीति सा द्वितीयां वित्त्वा न्यप्लवत ।
1.56.e: "Then seek a second one," he said; "verily not alone wilt thou sustain me." She, having found a second one, floated in.
1.56.m: He said: "Seek a second [verse]; alone you will not uphold me!" Having found a second, she floated back down.

1.56.s: icchasvaivety abravīn no vāva mā dve udyaṃsyatha iti sā tṛtīyāṃ vittvā nyaplavata so 'bravīd atra vai modyaṃsyatheti |
1.56.d: इच्छस्वैवेत्य् अब्रवीन् नो वाव मा द्वे उद्यंस्यथ इति सा तृतीयां वित्त्वा न्यप्लवत सो ऽब्रवीद् अत्र वै मोद्यंस्यथेति ।
1.56.e: " Seek a third one," lie said; " verily ye two will not sustain me." She, having found a third one, floated in. He said: "Verily now you will sustain me."
1.56.m: "Seek a third!" he said, "the two of you will surely not uphold me!" Having found a third, she floated back down. He said: "Now indeed you will uphold me!"

1.56.s: sa yad ekayāgre samavadata tasmād ekarce sāma atha yad dve apāsedhat tasmād dvayor na kurvanti atha yat tiṣṛbhis samapādayat tasmād u tṛce sāma |
1.56.d: स यद् एकयाग्रे समवदत तस्माद् एकर्चे साम अथ यद् द्वे अपासेधत् तस्माद् द्वयोर् न कुर्वन्ति अथ यत् तिषृभिस् समपादयत् तस्माद् उ तृचे साम ।
1.56.e: Because he talked first with one, therefore the sāman is in one re. And because he refused two, therefore they do not do (sing) it in two [ṛc's]. And because be agreed with three, therefore the sawaw is in a triplet,
1.56.m: Because he conversed with one in the beginning, therefore there is a sāman on a single verse. Then because he pushed away two, therefore they do not make [a sāman] on two. Then because he completed it with three, therefore the sāman is on a triplet.

1.56.s: tā abravīt punīdhvaṃ na pūtā vai stheti | aṣṭādaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.56.d: ता अब्रवीत् पुनीध्वं न पूता वै स्थेति । अष्टादशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
1.56.e: He said to them: "Cleanse yourselves, verily you are not clean."
1.56.m: He said to them: "Purify yourselves; you are not purified!" First khaṇḍa in the eighteenth anuvāka.

1.57.s: sā gāyatrī gāthayāpunīta nārāśaṃsyā triṣṭub raibhyā jagatī bhīmam bata malam apāvadhiṣateti tasmād bhīmalā dhiyo vā etāḥ dhiyo vā imā malam apāvadhiṣateti tasmād u bhīmalāḥ tasmād u gāyatāṃ nāśnīyāt malena hy ete jīvanti |
1.57.d: सा गायत्री गाथयापुनीत नाराशंस्या त्रिष्टुब् रैभ्या जगती भीमम् बत मलम् अपावधिषतेति तस्माद् भीमला धियो वा एताः धियो वा इमा मलम् अपावधिषतेति तस्माद् उ भीमलाः तस्माद् उ गायतां नाश्नीयात् मलेन ह्य् एते जीवन्ति ।
1.57.e: That gāyatrī cleansed itself with the gdthd, the tristubh with the ndrdfansi, the jagatl with the rdibhl. " Lo, they have struck away fearful (b'hlma) defilement (rnala)." Therefore these devices are terrible (? bhimala). " Verily, these devices have struck away defilement." And therefore [they are] terrible {? bhimala). And therefore one should not eat [anything] of those singing; for they live on defilement {m,ala).
1.57.m: The gāyatrī purified herself with a song (gāthā), the triṣṭubh with a nārāśaṃsī, the jagatī with a raibhī. "Alas, they have repelled terrible impurity!" Therefore these are terrible (bhīmalā) thoughts. "These thoughts have repelled impurity!" Therefore also they are terrible. Therefore one should not eat [food] of singers; for they live on impurity.

1.57.s: atha rk sāmābravīd bahu vai kiṃ ca kiṃ ca pumāṃś carati tvam anupunīṣveti sa ūrdhvagaṇenāpunīta |
1.57.d: अथ र्क् सामाब्रवीद् बहु वै किं च किं च पुमांश् चरति त्वम् अनुपुनीष्वेति स ऊर्ध्वगणेनापुनीत ।
1.57.e: Then the re said to the sāman: " Verily, much does a man pratice of this sort and of that. Cleanse thyself also." He cleansed himself with the upper series (?). 3. = I. 51. 1.
1.57.m: Then the ṛc said to the sāman: "A male wanders into much of whatever it may be. Purify yourself in turn!" He purified himself with the upward flock (ūrdhvagaṇa).

1.57.s: pūtāni ha vā asya sāmāni pūtā ṛcaḥ pūtāni yajūṃṣi pūtam anūktam pūtaṃ sarvam bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
1.57.d: पूतानि ह वा अस्य सामानि पूता ऋचः पूतानि यजूंषि पूतम् अनूक्तम् पूतं सर्वम् भवति य एवं वेद ।
1.57.m: Purified indeed are his sāmans, purified his ṛcs, purified his yajuses, purified what is recited after, purified everything becomes for him who knows thus.

1.57.s: tābhyāṃ diśo mithunāya paryauhan tāṃ sambhaviṣyann ahvayatāmo 'ham asmi sā tvaṃ sā tvam asy amo 'ham iti |
1.57.d: ताभ्यां दिशो मिथुनाय पर्यौहन् तां सम्भविष्यन्न् अह्वयतामो ऽहम् अस्मि सा त्वं सा त्वम् अस्य् अमो ऽहम् इति ।
1.57.e: They enclosed the quarters for their intercourse. When he was about to have intercourse with her, he called out: " I am he, thou art she; thou art she, 1 am he."
1.57.m: For them two they enclosed the directions for union. When he was about to unite with her, he called out: "I am he (ama), you are she (sā); you are she, I am he."

1.57.s: tām etad ubhayato vācātyaricyata hiṅkāreṇa purastāt stobhena madhyato nidhanenopariṣṭāt ati tisro brāhmaṇāyanīs sadṛśī ricyate ya evaṃ veda |
1.57.d: ताम् एतद् उभयतो वाचात्यरिच्यत हिङ्कारेण पुरस्तात् स्तोभेन मध्यतो निधनेनोपरिष्टात् अति तिस्रो ब्राह्मणायनीस् सदृशी रिच्यते य एवं वेद ।
1.57.e: With speech he thus exceeded her on both sides, with the hinkdra in front, with the stobha in the middle, with the nidhana in the rear. Three similar women of the Brahman caste exceeds he who knows thus.
1.57.m: He exceeded her on both sides with speech: with the hiṅkāra in front, with the stobha in the middle, with the nidhana at the end. He who knows thus surpasses three equal women of brahmin descent.

1.57.s: tayor yas sambhavator ūrdhvaś śūṣo 'dravat te te prāṇā evordhvā adravan |
1.57.d: तयोर् यस् सम्भवतोर् ऊर्ध्वश् शूषो ऽद्रवत् ते ते प्राणा एवोर्ध्वा अद्रवन् ।
1.57.e: The vital blast which when they had intercourse ran upward, that is the breaths. These breaths ran upward.
1.57.m: The upward vigor that ran forth from the two as they united, that was the breaths. Those breaths ran forth upwards.

1.57.s: so 'sāv ādityas sa eṣa eva ud agnir eva gī candramā eva tham sāmāny eva ud ṛca eva gī yajūṃṣy eva tham ity adhidevatam |
1.57.d: सो ऽसाव् आदित्यस् स एष एव उद् अग्निर् एव गी चन्द्रमा एव थम् सामान्य् एव उद् ऋच एव गी यजूंष्य् एव थम् इत्य् अधिदेवतम् ।
1.57.e: Yonder sun, that same is ud, Agni is gl, the moon is tham. The sāmans are ud, the ṛc's are gl, the yajuses are tham. So with regard to the divinities.
1.57.m: He is yonder sun; he is ud, Agni is gī, the Moon is tham; the sāmans are ud, the ṛcs are gī, the yajuses are tham—thus with respect to the deities.

1.57.s: athādhyātmam prāṇa eva ud vāg eva gī mana eva tham sa eṣo 'dhidevataṃ cādhyātmaṃ codgīthaḥ |
1.57.d: अथाध्यात्मम् प्राण एव उद् वाग् एव गी मन एव थम् स एषो ऽधिदेवतं चाध्यात्मं चोद्गीथः ।
1.57.e: Now with regard to the self. Breath is iid, speech is gl, mind is thain. That is this udgītha with regard both to the divinities and to the self.
1.57.m: Now with respect to the self: breath is ud, speech is gī, mind is tham. That is the udgītha both with respect to the deities and with respect to the self.

1.57.s: sa ya evam etad adhidevataṃ cādhyātmaṃ codgīthaṃ vedaitena hāsya sarveṇodgītam bhavaty etasmād u eva sarvasmād āvṛścyate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam upavadati | aṣṭādaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.57.d: स य एवम् एतद् अधिदेवतं चाध्यात्मं चोद्गीथं वेदैतेन हास्य सर्वेणोद्गीतम् भवत्य् एतस्माद् उ एव सर्वस्माद् आवृश्च्यते य एवं विद्वांसम् उपवदति । अष्टादशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
1.57.e: He who thus knows the tidgltha with regard both to the divinities and to the self, verily his udgītha is sung by this all; and he is cut off from this all who speaks ill of one who knows thus.
1.57.m: He who thus knows this udgītha with respect to the deities and with respect to the self, by all this it becomes sung up for him; and from all this is he cut off who speaks ill of one who knows thus. Second khaṇḍa in the eighteenth anuvāka.

1.58.s: tad yad idam āhuḥ ka udagāsīr iti ka etam ādityam agāsīr iti ha vā etat pṛcchanti |
1.58.d: तद् यद् इदम् आहुः क उदगासीर् इति क एतम् आदित्यम् अगासीर् इति ह वा एतत् पृच्छन्ति ।
1.58.e: When they say here: "As who hast thou sung the udgītha?" they ask this: "As who hast thou sung this sun?"
1.58.m: As to what they say, "Which [chanter] did you sing up?"—"Which [chanter] sang this sun?" is what they ask.

1.58.s: etaṃ ha vā etaṃ trayyā vidyayā gāyanti yathā vīṇāgāthino gāpayeyur evam |
1.58.d: एतं ह वा एतं त्रय्या विद्यया गायन्ति यथा वीणागाथिनो गापयेयुर् एवम् ।
1.58.e: Verily they sing it with the threefold knowledge, just as lute-players might play.
1.58.m: Him indeed they sing with the triple knowledge, just as lute-singers would have someone sing.

1.58.s: sa eṣa hradaḥ kāmānām pūrṇo yan manaḥ tasyaiṣā kulyā yad vāk |
1.58.d: स एष ह्रदः कामानाम् पूर्णो यन् मनः तस्यैषा कुल्या यद् वाक् ।
1.58.e: Mind is this pool full of desires. Speech is the stream of it.
1.58.m: That which is the mind is this lake filled with desires. That which is speech is its watercourse.

1.58.s: tad yathā vā apo hradāt kulyayoparām upanayanty evam evaitan manaso 'dhi vācodgātā yajamānam yasya kāmān prayacchati |
1.58.d: तद् यथा वा अपो ह्रदात् कुल्ययोपराम् उपनयन्त्य् एवम् एवैतन् मनसो ऽधि वाचोद्गाता यजमानम् यस्य कामान् प्रयच्छति ।
1.58.e: As they lead the water from a lake nearer by means of a stream, just so the udgdtar [leads] that from the mind by means of speech unto the sacrificer whose wishes he fulfils.
1.58.m: Then just as they lead waters from a lake to lower ground through a watercourse, so indeed does the udgātṛ, through speech, grant the desires of the sacrificer from the mind.

1.58.s: sa ya udgātāraṃ dakṣiṇābhir ārādhayati taṃ sā kulyopadhāvati ya u enaṃ nārādhayati sa u tām apihanti |
1.58.d: स य उद्गातारं दक्षिणाभिर् आराधयति तं सा कुल्योपधावति य उ एनं नाराधयति स उ ताम् अपिहन्ति ।
1.58.e: Whoso by sacrificial gifts conciliates the udgdtar, unto him this stream runs; and whoso does not conciliate him, he drives this [stream] away.
1.58.m: He who pleases the udgātṛ with sacrificial gifts, towards him runs that watercourse. And he who does not please him, he dams it up.

1.58.s: atha vā ataḥ prattiś caiva pratigrahaś ca tad dhūmam iti vai pradīyate tad vācā yajamānāya pradeyam manasātmane tathā ha sarvaṃ na prayacchati |
1.58.d: अथ वा अतः प्रत्तिश् चैव प्रतिग्रहश् च तद् धूमम् इति वै प्रदीयते तद् वाचा यजमानाय प्रदेयम् मनसात्मने तथा ह सर्वं न प्रयच्छति ।
1.58.e: Now henceforth [about] giving and receiving. [A gift] is given [with the words]: " This is smoke." Thus it should be given to the sacrificer with speech, with the mind to one's self. Thus one does not bestow all.
1.58.m: Now, then, of giving and receiving: "Take this!"—thus indeed it is given. That should be given to the sacrificer through speech, and to oneself through the mind. Thus indeed he does not give away everything.

1.58.s: tad yad idaṃ sambhavato reto 'sicyata tad aśayat yathā hiraṇyam avikṛtaṃ lelāyad evam |
1.58.d: तद् यद् इदं सम्भवतो रेतो ऽसिच्यत तद् अशयत् यथा हिरण्यम् अविकृतं लेलायद् एवम् ।
1.58.e: That seed which was shed when they had intercourse, that lay there, just like undefiled sparkling gold.
1.58.m: That seed which was emitted from the two as they united lay there like unworked gold, trembling.

1.58.s: tasya sarve devā mamatvina āsan mama mameti te 'bruvan vīdaṃ karavāmahā iti te 'bruvañ chreyo vā idam asmat ātmabhir evainad vikaravāmahā iti |
1.58.d: तस्य सर्वे देवा ममत्विन आसन् मम ममेति ते ऽब्रुवन् वीदं करवामहा इति ते ऽब्रुवञ् छ्रेयो वा इदम् अस्मत् आत्मभिर् एवैनद् विकरवामहा इति ।
1.58.e: Of it all the gods were desirous to be possessors [saying]: " It is mine, it is mine." They said: "Let us divide it among ourselves." They said:" Verily, it is superior to us. Let us divide it by our selves."
1.58.m: All the gods claimed ownership of it, [saying,] “Mine! Mine!” They said: “Let us divide this.” They said: “This is indeed better than us. Let us divide it through our own selves.”

1.58.s: tad ātmabhir eva vyakurvata teṣāṃ vāyur eva hiṅkāra āsāgniḥ prastāva indra ādis somabṛhaspatī udgītho 'śvinau pratihāro viśve devā upadravaḥ prajāpatir eva nidhanam |
1.58.d: तद् आत्मभिर् एव व्यकुर्वत तेषां वायुर् एव हिङ्कार आसाग्निः प्रस्ताव इन्द्र आदिस् सोमबृहस्पती उद्गीथो ऽश्विनौ प्रतिहारो विश्वे देवा उपद्रवः प्रजापतिर् एव निधनम् ।
1.58.e: They divided it by their selves. Of them Vayu was the hinkdra, Agni the prOjStdva, Indra the ddi. Soma and Brhaspati the udgītha, the two Agvins the pratihāra, all the gods the upadrava, Prajapati the nidhana.
1.58.m: They divided it through their own selves: of them, Vāyu was the hiṅkāra; Agni the prastāva; Indra the ādi; Soma and Bṛhaspati the udgītha; the Aśvins the pratihāra; the Viśve Devas the upadrava; Prajāpati alone the nidhana.

1.58.s: etā vai sarvā devatā etā hiraṇyam asya sarvābhir devatābhis stutam bhavati ya evaṃ veda etābhya u eva sa sarvābhyo devatābhya āvṛścyate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam upavadati | aṣṭādaśe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.58.d: एता वै सर्वा देवता एता हिरण्यम् अस्य सर्वाभिर् देवताभिस् स्तुतम् भवति य एवं वेद एताभ्य उ एव स सर्वाभ्यो देवताभ्य आवृश्च्यते य एवं विद्वांसम् उपवदति । अष्टादशे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
1.58.e: Verily these are all the divinities; these are gold. Praised by all divinities it is of him who knows thus; and from all divinities he is cut off who speaks ill of one who knows thus.
1.58.m: These indeed are all the deities; these are the gold. Praise is chanted by all the deities for him who knows thus. And he who speaks ill of one who knows thus is cut off from all these deities. The third section in the eighteenth lesson.

1.59.s: atha ha brahmadattaś caikitāneyaḥ kuruṃ jagāmābhipratāriṇaṃ kākṣasenim sa hāsmai madhuparkaṃ yayāca |
1.59.d: अथ ह ब्रह्मदत्तश् चैकितानेयः कुरुं जगामाभिप्रतारिणं काक्षसेनिम् स हास्मै मधुपर्कं ययाच ।
1.59.e: Now Brahmadatta Caikitaneya went to the Kuru Abhipratarin Kaksaseni. He (A.) offered him a honey-potion [madhuparka). -j. Now his purohita Śaunaka, stepping forth, sat down near by. He (B.) drank the honey-potion without addressing him (^.).
1.59.m: Now Brahmadatta Caikitāneya went to the Kuru Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni. He requested the honey-mixture of him.

1.59.s: atha hāsya vai prapadya purohito 'nte niṣasāda śaunakaḥ taṃ hānāmantrya madhuparkam papau |
1.59.d: अथ हास्य वै प्रपद्य पुरोहितो ऽन्ते निषसाद शौनकः तं हानामन्त्र्य मधुपर्कम् पपौ ।
1.59.m: Then his purohita Śaunaka, approaching, sat down nearby. Without addressing him, [Brahmadatta] drank the honey-mixture.

1.59.s: taṃ hovāca kiṃ vidvān no dālbhyānāmantrya madhuparkam pibasīti sāmavairyam prapadyeti hovāca |
1.59.d: तं होवाच किं विद्वान् नो दाल्भ्यानामन्त्र्य मधुपर्कम् पिबसीति सामवैर्यम् प्रपद्येति होवाच ।
1.59.e: He {Q.) said to him (B.): "As knowing what, O Dalbhya, dost thou drink the honey-potion without addressing [me]?" " Having recourse to that which belongs to the strength of the sāman (?)," he (B.) said.
1.59.m: He said to him: “Knowing what, O Dālbhya, do you drink the honey-mixture without addressing us?” He said: “Having resort to the heroism of the sāman.”

1.59.s: taṃ ha tatraiva papraccha yad vāyau tad vetthā3 iti hiṅkāro vā asya sa iti |
1.59.d: तं ह तत्रैव पप्रच्छ यद् वायौ तद् वेत्था3 इति हिङ्कारो वा अस्य स इति ।
1.59.e: He {(}.) asked him (B.) just there: " Dost thou know that which is in Vayu?" "Verily, the hinkdra of it."
1.59.m: He asked him right there: “Do you know that which is in Vāyu?” [Brahmadatta replied:] “That is indeed its hiṅkāra.”

1.59.s: yad agnau tad vetthā3 iti prastāvo vā asya sa iti |
1.59.d: यद् अग्नौ तद् वेत्था3 इति प्रस्तावो वा अस्य स इति ।
1.59.e: "Dost thou know that which is in Agni?" " Verily, the prastāva of it."
1.59.m: “Do you know that which is in Agni?” “That is indeed its prastāva.”

1.59.s: yad indre tad vetthā3 iti ādir vā asya sa iti |
1.59.d: यद् इन्द्रे तद् वेत्था3 इति आदिर् वा अस्य स इति ।
1.59.e: " Dost thou know that which is in Indra?" "Verily, the atZiof it."
1.59.m: “Do you know that which is in Indra?” “That is indeed its ādi.”

1.59.s: yat somabṛhaspatyos tad vetthā3 iti udgītho vā asya sa iti |
1.59.d: यत् सोमबृहस्पत्योस् तद् वेत्था3 इति उद्गीथो वा अस्य स इति ।
1.59.e: "Dost thou know that which is in Soma and Brhaspati?" " Verily, the udgitha of it."
1.59.m: “Do you know that which is in Soma and Bṛhaspati?” “That is indeed its udgītha.”

1.59.s: yad aśvinos tad vetthā3 iti pratihāro vā asya sa iti |
1.59.d: यद् अश्विनोस् तद् वेत्था3 इति प्रतिहारो वा अस्य स इति ।
1.59.e: " Dost thou know that which is in the two A5vins?" " Verily, the praiihdra of it."
1.59.m: “Do you know that which is in the Aśvins?” “That is indeed its pratihāra.”

1.59.s: yad viśveṣu deveṣu tad vetthā3 iti upadravo vā asya sa iti |
1.59.d: यद् विश्वेषु देवेषु तद् वेत्था3 इति उपद्रवो वा अस्य स इति ।
1.59.e: Dost thou know that which is in all the gods?" " Verily, the upadrava of it."
1.59.m: “Do you know that which is in the Viśve Devas?” “That is indeed its upadrava.”

1.59.s: yat prajāpatau tad vetthā3 iti nidhanaṃ vā asya tad iti hovāca ārṣeyaṃ vā asya tad bandhutā vā asya seti |
1.59.d: यत् प्रजापतौ तद् वेत्था3 इति निधनं वा अस्य तद् इति होवाच आर्षेयं वा अस्य तद् बन्धुता वा अस्य सेति ।
1.59.e: " Dost thou know that which is in Prajapati?" " Verily, the nidhana of it," he said; "that of it belongs to the sages (rsi); that is its connection."
1.59.m: “Do you know that which is in Prajāpati?” He said: “That is indeed its nidhana. That is its ancestral lineage, that is its kinship.”

1.59.s: sa hovāca namas te 'stu bhagavo vidvān apā madhuparkam iti |
1.59.d: स होवाच नमस् ते ऽस्तु भगवो विद्वान् अपा मधुपर्कम् इति ।
1.59.e: He {().) said: "Homage be to thee, reverend sir; with knowledge hast thou drunk the honey-potion."
1.59.m: He said: “Homage be to you, reverend sir! Knowing, you have drunk the honey-mixture.”

1.59.s: atha hetaraḥ papraccha kiṃdevatyaṃ sāmavairyam prapadyeti yaddevatyāsu stuvata iti hovāca taddevatyam iti |
1.59.d: अथ हेतरः पप्रच्छ किंदेवत्यं सामवैर्यम् प्रपद्येति यद्देवत्यासु स्तुवत इति होवाच तद्देवत्यम् इति ।
1.59.e: Then the other one (A.) asked: " What divinities has that which belongs to the strength of the sāman (?) to which thou hast recourse?" " What divinities the [vei'ses] have with which the praise [stotra) is sung," he (B.) said, " those it has as divinities."
1.59.m: Then the other asked: “Having resort to the heroism of the sāman, to what deity does it belong?” He said: “To whatever deity [the verses belong] on which they chant praise, to that deity does it belong.”

1.59.s: tad etat sādhv eva pratyuktam vyāptir vā asyaiṣeti hovāca brūhy eveti medaṃ te namo 'karmeti hovāca maiva no 'tiprākṣīr iti |
1.59.d: तद् एतत् साध्व् एव प्रत्युक्तम् व्याप्तिर् वा अस्यैषेति होवाच ब्रूह्य् एवेति मेदं ते नमो ऽकर्मेति होवाच मैव नो ऽतिप्राक्षीर् इति ।
1.59.e: "That was well answered; that is its accomplishment (?)," he said; "just talk." "Don't! We have done thee this honor," he said; " do not ask us too much."
1.59.m: “That has indeed been properly answered. This is its pervasive reach,” he said; “Speak on!” He said: “Let us not make this homage to you! Do not question us too far!”

1.59.s: sa hovācāprakṣyaṃ vāva tvā devatām aprakṣyaṃ vāva tvā devatāyai devatāḥ vāgdevatyaṃ sāma vāco mano devatā manasaḥ paśavaḥ paśūnām oṣadhaya oṣadhīnām āpaḥ tad etad adbhyo jātaṃ sāmāpsu pratiṣṭhitam iti | aṣṭādaśe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
1.59.d: स होवाचाप्रक्ष्यं वाव त्वा देवताम् अप्रक्ष्यं वाव त्वा देवतायै देवताः वाग्देवत्यं साम वाचो मनो देवता मनसः पशवः पशूनाम् ओषधय ओषधीनाम् आपः तद् एतद् अद्भ्यो जातं सामाप्सु प्रतिष्ठितम् इति । अष्टादशे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
1.59.e: He said: " I should have asked thee about the divinity, I should have asked thee about the divinities of the divinity. The sāman has speech as its divinity; mind is the divinity of speech, the domestic animals [are the divinity] of mind, the herbs [are the divinity] of the domestic animals, the waters [are the divinity] of the herbs. That same is the sāman born from the waters, standing firm in the waters."
1.59.m: He said: “I would indeed have questioned you about the deity; I would indeed have questioned you about the deities of the deity. Speech is the deity of the sāman; mind is the deity of speech; cattle [are the deity] of mind; plants [are the deity] of cattle; waters [are the deity] of plants. This sāman, born from the waters, is established in the waters.” The fourth section in the eighteenth lesson.

1.60.s: devāsurā aspardhanta te devā manasodagāyan tad eṣām asurā abhidrutya pāpmanā samasṛjan tasmād bahu kiṃ ca kiṃ ca manasā dhyāyati puṇyaṃ cainena dhyāyati pāpaṃ ca |
1.60.d: देवासुरा अस्पर्धन्त ते देवा मनसोदगायन् तद् एषाम् असुरा अभिद्रुत्य पाप्मना समसृजन् तस्माद् बहु किं च किं च मनसा ध्यायति पुण्यं चैनेन ध्यायति पापं च ।
1.60.e: The gods and the Asuras contended. The gods sang the udgWia with the mind. The Asuras, running against this [mind] of them, mixed it with evil. Therefore with the mind one thinks many a thing of one kind and another; both [what is] good one thinks with it and [what; is] evil.
1.60.m: The gods and the asuras contended. Those gods chanted the udgītha with the mind. Rushing at it, the asuras contaminated it with evil. Therefore with the mind one thinks much of whatever; and with it one thinks good and bad.

1.60.s: te vācodagāyan tāṃ tathaivākurvan tasmād bahu kiṃ ca kiṃ ca vācā vadati satyaṃ cainayā vadaty anṛtaṃ ca |
1.60.d: ते वाचोदगायन् तां तथैवाकुर्वन् तस्माद् बहु किं च किं च वाचा वदति सत्यं चैनया वदत्य् अनृतं च ।
1.60.e: They sang the udgitha with speech. That [speech] they treated in just the same way. Therefore with speech one speaks many a thing of this kind and of that; both [what is] true one speaks with it and what is] untrue.
1.60.m: They chanted the udgītha with speech. They did the very same to it. Therefore with speech one speaks much of whatever; and with it one speaks truth and falsehood.

1.60.s: te cakṣuṣodagāyan tat tathaivākurvan tasmād bahu kiṃ ca kiṃ ca cakṣuṣā paśyati darśanīyaṃ cainena paśyaty adarśanīyaṃ ca |
1.60.d: ते चक्षुषोदगायन् तत् तथैवाकुर्वन् तस्माद् बहु किं च किं च चक्षुषा पश्यति दर्शनीयं चैनेन पश्यत्य् अदर्शनीयं च ।
1.60.e: They sang the udgītha with sight. That sight] they treated in just the same manner. Therefore with sight one sees many a thing of this kind and of that; both [what is] seemly one sees with it and [what is] unseemly.
1.60.m: They chanted the udgītha with sight. They did the very same to it. Therefore with sight one sees much of whatever; and with it one sees what is sightly and what is unsightly.

1.60.s: te śrotreṇodagāyan tat tathaivākurvan tasmād bahu kiṃ ca kiṃ ca śrotreṇa śṛṇoti śravaṇīyaṃ cainena śṛṇoty aśravaṇīyaṃ ca |
1.60.d: ते श्रोत्रेणोदगायन् तत् तथैवाकुर्वन् तस्माद् बहु किं च किं च श्रोत्रेण शृणोति श्रवणीयं चैनेन शृणोत्य् अश्रवणीयं च ।
1.60.e: They sang the udgītha with hearing. That [hearing] they treated in just the same manner. Therefore with hearing one hears many a thing of this kind and of that; both [what is] worth hearing one hears with it and [what is] not worth hearing.
1.60.m: They chanted the udgītha with hearing. They did the very same to it. Therefore with hearing one hears much of whatever; and with it one hears what is worth hearing and what is not worth hearing.

1.60.s: te 'pānenodagāyan taṃ tathaivākurvan tasmād bahu kiṃ ca kiṃ cāpānena jighrati surabhi cainena jighrati durgandhi ca |
1.60.d: ते ऽपानेनोदगायन् तं तथैवाकुर्वन् तस्माद् बहु किं च किं चापानेन जिघ्रति सुरभि चैनेन जिघ्रति दुर्गन्धि च ।
1.60.e: They sang the udgUha with exhalation. That [exhalation] they treated in just the same manner. Therefore with exhalation one smells many a thing of this kind and of that; both what is fragrant one smells with it and what is of bad odor.
1.60.m: They chanted the udgītha with the downward breath. They did the very same to it. Therefore with the downward breath one smells much of whatever; and with it one smells what is fragrant and what is foul-smelling.

1.60.s: te prāṇenodagāyan athāsurā ādravaṃs tathā kariṣyāma iti manyamānāḥ |
1.60.d: ते प्राणेनोदगायन् अथासुरा आद्रवंस् तथा करिष्याम इति मन्यमानाः ।
1.60.e: They sang the udgītha with breath. Then the Asuras ran up, thinking: " We will treat it in the same manner."
1.60.m: They chanted the udgītha with breath. Then the asuras rushed up, thinking, “We will do likewise.”

1.60.s: sa yathāśmānam ṛtvā loṣṭo vidhvaṃsetaivam evāsurā vyadhvaṃsanta sa eṣo 'śmākhaṇaṃ yat prāṇaḥ |
1.60.d: स यथाश्मानम् ऋत्वा लोष्टो विध्वंसेतैवम् एवासुरा व्यध्वंसन्त स एषो ऽश्माखणं यत् प्राणः ।
1.60.e: As a clod of earth colliding with a stone would break to pieces, even so the Asuras broke to pieces. Breath is this stone as a tai-get.
1.60.m: Just as a clod of earth, striking against a stone, would shatter, so indeed the asuras shattered. Breath is this solid stone.

1.60.s: sa yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā loṣṭo vidhvaṃsata evam eva sa vidhvaṃsate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsam upavadati | aṣṭādaśe 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ aṣṭādaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
1.60.d: स यथाश्मानम् आखणम् ऋत्वा लोष्टो विध्वंसत एवम् एव स विध्वंसते य एवं विद्वांसम् उपवदति । अष्टादशे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः अष्टादशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
1.60.e: As a clod of earth, colliding with a stone as a target, breaks to pieces, even so he breaks to pieces who speaks ill of one who knows thus.
1.60.m: Just as a clod of earth, striking against a solid stone, shatters, so indeed he shatters who speaks ill of one who knows thus. The fifth section in the eighteenth lesson. The eighteenth lesson is complete.
